author: r6e
body:
## Summary

Adds the encoding batch of the expanded built-in function set (Phase 2): `json.marshal`, `json.unmarshal`, `json.is_valid`, `base64.encode/decode/is_valid`, `base64url.encode/decode`, `hex.encode/decode`, `urlquery.encode/decode`. All semantics verified empirically against **OPA 1.17**.

```rego
package example
doc   := json.marshal(input.obj)        # sorted keys, sets as sorted arrays, Go-style HTML escaping
val   := json.unmarshal(input.json)
token := base64.encode(input.secret)
hexed := hex.encode(input.secret)
query := urlquery.encode(input.raw)
```

## What changed

- **`lib/ruby/rego/builtins/codecs.rb`** — new `Builtins::Codecs` category (configured-functions registry pattern), wired into `lib/ruby/rego.rb`.
- `json.marshal` sorts object keys, emits compact JSON, renders sets as **element-wise-sorted** arrays, and applies Go's HTML escaping (`<`,`>`,`&`,U+2028,U+2029 → `\uXXXX`). `json.unmarshal`/`json.is_valid` parse JSON.
- `base64`/`base64url`/`hex`/`urlquery` encode/decode. Standard base64 decode is strict; base64url decode tolerates missing padding (like OPA). `hex.decode` rejects non-hex/odd-length. `urlquery` matches Go's `url.QueryEscape`/`QueryUnescape` via `CGI`, including rejecting malformed percent-escapes.
- Invalid/un-marshalable input yields an **undefined** result (never a raised error): invalid decoder input, non-finite numbers, over-deep JSON nesting, and NaN-in-set all degrade gracefully.
- Declares `base64`, `cgi`, `json` as runtime dependencies (default gems now separately installable). RBS, unit + integration specs, README/CHANGELOG/TODO.

## Verification

- **510 examples, 0 failures, 0 pending**; coverage 94.33%. Steep, RuboCop, Reek all clean.
- Semantics cross-validated against `opa eval` 1.17 across ~40 cases (key sorting, HTML escaping, composite/mixed/nested set ordering, base64 strict-vs-lenient, hex validation, urlquery Go-parity, malformed-percent decode).
- The adversarial review panel cycled to convergence over multiple full-panel rounds and caught a series of real `json.marshal` robustness bugs — all fixed:
  - **HTML escaping** missing (`<a>&b` now `<a>&b`).
  - **Composite set ordering** by serialized string instead of element-wise (`{[2],[10]}` now `[[2],[10]]`).
  - **Three crash paths** where un-marshalable values raised uncaught exceptions instead of undefined: non-finite numbers (`JSON::GeneratorError`), over-deep nesting (`JSON::NestingError`), and NaN-in-set (sort `ArgumentError`). `json.marshal` now rescues both `JSON::JSONError` and `ArgumentError`.
  - **`urlquery.decode`** of malformed percent-escapes (`%ZZ`, `%2`) now returns undefined (matching Go), where `CGI.unescape` had passed them through.
  - Added `base64.is_valid` (OPA parity).
- Several reviewer-claimed divergences were **empirically disproven** against OPA and correctly not "fixed" (would have introduced divergences): `urlquery.encode("~")` (both preserve `~`), `base64url.encode` padding (both padded), and `is_valid`-returns-false-on-non-string (OPA raises a type error).

## Documented divergences / limitations

- Patterns/values that can't be represented yield **undefined**: non-finite numbers and JSON nested beyond Ruby's default depth (a deliberate DoS safeguard) — OPA processes deeper structures.
- A pathologically deep value (~10k+ levels) raises an uncatchable `SystemStackError` at `Value.from_ruby` construction — a **pre-existing, evaluator-wide** recursion limitation (not encoding-specific; OPA bounds this via a nesting limit). Tracked in `TODO.md` as a shared-depth-guard follow-up.

## Deferred (tracked in TODO)

- `yaml.*`, `urlquery.encode_object`/`decode_object`, `base64url.encode_no_pad`.
- Extract a shared `Builtins::StringHelpers.string_value` (de-duplicate `string_arg` across `codecs.rb` + `regex.rb`).

## Test plan

- [ ] `bundle exec rspec` — 510 examples, 0 failures
- [ ] `bundle exec steep check` — 0 diagnostics
- [ ] `bundle exec rubocop` && `bundle exec reek lib` — clean
- [ ] Spot-check encoding builtins against `opa eval`

## Summary

Closes **audit G18** + **G22** from `UX_UI_AUDIT_2026-06-02.md` (the refreshed audit doc itself is also included in this PR with the retrospective correction).

- **G18 — ProjectHeaderCard de-emphasis.** Status badges now lead the chip row so the actual urgency signal wins the eye. The three descriptive Tags (projectClass / deliveryMethod / contractingModel) drop their colored fills and render as neutral `<Tag>`s; AntD algorithm tokens handle the dark-mode adaptation. **Scoped to the hero card** per the audit — `ProjectsTable` and Gantt retain their semantic color encoding intentionally (different visual context, the goal there is data scanning not urgency framing).
- **G22 — SCurveChart adopts the helper.** Extends `chart-helpers.todayMarkLine` with optional `color` (applied uniformly to the line + label) and `labelFontWeight` options. `SCurveChart` now consumes the helper via `{ ...todayMarkLine({ label, color, labelFontWeight: 'bold' }), data: [{ xAxis: lastIndex }] }`. Visual identity preserved. The helper finally has a non-test production consumer.

## D2 retrospective — dropping the wrong recommendation

The morning audit recommended `fix(d2): block negative budgetImpact in CR create modal`. The refreshed audit (afternoon) propagated that into the Tier-1 bundle as PR 1. **Both audits were wrong:**

- `src/types/document.ts:144` — `budgetImpact: number` (signed, no constraint)
- `src/data/change-requests.json:49` — one seeded CR has `"budgetImpact": -50000`
- `ChangeRequestHistoryTable.tsx:50-58` — positive rendered red with `+` prefix (cost increase); negative rendered green (cost savings). The author deliberately encoded the savings semantics.

Construction-domain reality: descope CRs, value-engineering CRs, and contingency-release CRs all produce negative budget deltas. Blocking negative would break the seeded demo and remove a real workflow. PR 1 dropped from the bundle; **D2 is now fully shipped**.

`UX_UI_AUDIT_2026-06-02.md` Part 3/4 updated and Appendix B gains a new retrospective entry with the verify-against-domain-type / seed-data / downstream-renderer pre-flight rule for future audits.

body:
## Symptom
`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')` at `TechnicalWorkspace.tsx` (inside the `technicalPrepChecklist.map`) — crashes the whole Technical-stage prep view via the error boundary.

## Root cause (cross-repo type drift)
The UI read `item.resources`, but the Coach Agent contract (ai-applications `strategist-types.ts:640`) **and** the persisted `coaching_content` JSON use **`suggestedResources`**. The tucaken-app `TechnicalPrepItem` type declared `resources`, so `item.resources` was always `undefined` → `.length` threw whenever a technical prep had a non-empty checklist (deterministic).

Confirmed on dev: stored `technicalPrepChecklist[0]` keys = `topic, priority, rationale, suggestedResources`.

Tests didn't catch it: every fixture used `technicalPrepChecklist: []` (empty), so an item was never rendered.

## Fix
- Rename `TechnicalPrepItem.resources` → `suggestedResources` (matches the contract).
- `TechnicalWorkspace` reads `item.suggestedResources`, guarded (`item.suggestedResources && …`) for defense-in-depth.
- New render test exercising a **non-empty** checklist (the previously-uncovered path).

## Scope check
Diffed all coach-output field names across both repos — `suggestedResources` was the **only** drift; InterviewQuestion / DifficultQuestion / QuestionToAsk / PhoneScreenTalkingPoint / CompScript all match. No other latent crash of this kind.

## Verification
`tsc --noEmit` clean; stage-components tests **48/48** (was 47 + the new regression test).

## What does this PR do?

Enriches the GUI **Profiles** page so a profile is a first-class, self-describing workspace instead of just a name, and removes credential duplication between the **Keys/Env** and **Channels** pages.

Profiles page now supports:
- **Active profile switching** — view the sticky active profile (`hermes profile use`) vs. the profile the running dashboard is scoped to, and set a new active profile inline.
- **Role descriptions** — set/clear a description manually, or auto-generate one via the auxiliary LLM (`auxiliary.profile_describer`). Descriptions double as the routing signal for kanban tasks.
- **Per-profile model selection** — assign `model.provider` + `model.default` for a specific profile without retargeting the dashboard's own active profile (scoped via the `HERMES_HOME` override).
- **Status & metadata badges** — gateway-running state, distribution name/version/source, and alias indicators.

author: sridhar-3009
body:
## Problem

Closes #116.

`song_to_music_dto` resolved the display artist by checking `song.album_artists` first. For compilation albums — where `album_artist` is "Various Artists" — every track showed "Various Artists" instead of the actual performer. The bug also affected the MPRIS metadata that media players and desktop environments read.

## Root cause

```rust
// Before — album_artists checked FIRST
let artist_name = song
    .album_artists.first().map(|a| a.name.clone())   // "Various Artists" ← wins
    .or(fallback.album_artists.first().map(...))
    .or(song.album_artist)
    .or(song.artist)    // "PSYQUI" ← never reached
    ...
```

## Fix

Reorder the chain to prefer the track-level artist:

```rust
// After — song.artist checked FIRST
let artist_name = song
    .artist                                           // "PSYQUI" ← correct
    .or(song.album_artist)
    .or_else(|| song.album_artists.first().map(...))  // "Various Artists" ← fallback
    ...
```

Same reordering applied to `artist_id` so the name and ID remain consistent.

Since `MusicDto.album_artists` stores the resolved artist name, both the UI label and MPRIS metadata now show the correct per-track performer.

## Problem

The object storage client in `objectStorage.ts` was hardcoded to Replit's local sidecar endpoint (`http://127.0.0.1:1106`) for both authentication and presigned URL generation. On Railway this sidecar does not exist, causing every call to `getObjectEntityUploadURL` to fail with "Error generating upload URL".

## Solution

Replaced `@google-cloud/storage` and `google-auth-library` with `@aws-sdk/client-s3` and `@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner`. The new `S3Client` is configured from Railway's bucket environment variables (`ENDPOINT`, `REGION`, `ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`). Presigned PUT URLs are now generated via `getSignedUrl` from the AWS presigner. All methods that previously accepted a GCS `File` object now use a plain `S3ObjectRef` interface (`{ bucketName, objectName }`), and `objectAcl.ts` was updated in parallel to use `HeadObjectCommand`/`CopyObjectCommand` for metadata reads and writes.

author: leoborcherding
body:
## Summary

Two bugs affecting RDNA2 GPUs (gfx1030-gfx1036, e.g. RX 6600/6700/6800/6900) when ROCm 7.x is installed:

**Bug 1 — Installer puts a dev/nightly PyTorch build in the Studio venv**

When ROCm 7.x is detected, the installer selects the `rocm7.x` PyTorch index which serves dev builds (version string contains a git hash, e.g. `2.10.0+rocm7.2.0.gitb6ee5fde`). These builds segfault during unsloth's import/patching phase on RDNA2 hardware. The user's system pip had a stable `2.7.1+rocm6.2.4` but the Studio venv got the broken dev build.

Fix: detect the runtime GPU gfx code at install time. If it's RDNA2, cap the torch install to the `rocm6.2` index (torch 2.7.x) regardless of system ROCm version. Applied in both `install.sh` and `install_python_stack.py`, with `--force-reinstall` so existing broken builds get replaced.

**Bug 2 — Inference subprocess crashes with LLVM ERROR on RDNA2**

The training path fix from #5301 only covered `trainer.py`. The inference subprocess (`InferenceBackend.load_model()`) still passed `dtype=None` to `FastLanguageModel/FastVisionModel.from_pretrained()`, which auto-selected bfloat16 on RDNA2, triggering:
```
LLVM ERROR: Cannot select: intrinsic %llvm.amdgcn.fdot2.bf16.bf16
```

Fix: apply the same `is_bfloat16_supported()` guard from `trainer.py` to `InferenceBackend.load_model()`, forcing `float16` on hardware that doesn't support bfloat16.

## Files changed

- `install.sh` — RDNA2 gfx detection + rocm6.2 cap in the shell installer
- `studio/install_python_stack.py` — same cap in the Python stack installer (`unsloth studio update`)
- `studio/backend/core/inference/inference.py` — float16 fallback for inference on RDNA2

Closes https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth/issues/5337

author: nhwalker
body:
## What

Move the virtual display (Xvfb) out of the app/test image and into a **separate sidecar container** that shares its `/tmp/.X11-unix` socket with the app container via a Docker volume.

This was a question — "what if we didn't include Xvfb in the test harness; can we run it in a second container and share the X socket?" — and the answer is yes. It's also **more faithful to production**: the production image has no X server of its own and attaches to one running *outside* the container (see `launch.sh`'s notes about mounting `/tmp/.X11-unix`). The sidecar mirrors exactly that model.

## Why it's nicer

- The app/harness image carries **no display tooling** — only ChromeDriver is layered on the production image.
- Display provisioning is decoupled from the app, and the test exercises the real "connect to an external X server over a shared socket" path.

## How it works

- `xvfb.Dockerfile` / `xvfb-entrypoint.sh` — a tiny Debian-based sidecar running `Xvfb :99 -ac`, which clears any stale socket, publishes a fresh one into the shared volume, and announces `X-READY`.
- `harness.Dockerfile` — drops the `Xvfb` install; adds only the version-matched ChromeDriver.
- `test-harness-entrypoint.sh` — waits for the shared X socket (instead of starting Xvfb), then launches the real app via the production `/app/launch.sh` with remote debugging, then exposes ChromeDriver.
- `ElectronAppFunctionalTest` — starts the Xvfb sidecar + app container, both mounting a shared named volume at `/tmp/.X11-unix` (via a create-command modifier, since `withVolumesFrom` resolves the source name too eagerly for static fields). The app container `dependsOn` the sidecar and sets `DISPLAY=:99`. Assertions now also check the UA reports the **X11** backend, confirming it's rendering on the shared display.

Everything else from the previous change is unchanged: the test still builds the **production image** and the app still falls back to **software rendering** on a GPU-less host (the NVIDIA stack stays inert).

## Verification

Ran the full suite locally against a real Docker daemon — all green:

```
BrowserContainerFunctionalTest > Chromium renders a page served from a sibling container   PASSED
ElectronAppFunctionalTest > The production app renders a page via a sidecar X server…       PASSED
StackSmokeTest > Runs on a Java 25 toolchain                                                PASSED
StackSmokeTest > Core test libraries are on the classpath                                   PASSED
```

I also confirmed manually that the `X99` socket is created by the sidecar and seen identically in the app container via the shared volume, and that the app's UA is `...electron-gpu-test/1.0.0 ... Electron/41.1.1 ... (X11; Linux x86_64)`.

## Notes / defaults chosen

- Sidecar uses `Xvfb -ac` (access control off) so the app container needs no xauth cookie over the shared socket; the socket is `chmod 0777`'d for the app's non-root uid.
- The shared volume uses a fixed name (`electron-gpu-test-xsock`); the sidecar removes any stale socket on start, so reuse across runs is safe. A unique-per-run name would avoid all chance of collision but would leak volumes (not Ryuk-labeled) — I judged the fixed name the better default.
- The Xvfb sidecar base image is pulled from the AWS ECR public Docker Hub mirror to avoid Hub pull-rate limits in CI.

author: cloudurbane
body:
…A sessions

users.token is a uuid column, so a legacy/non-UUID scent_token left in a browser's localStorage made Postgres throw "invalid input syntax for type uuid" on every protected request — surfacing as an unrecoverable 500. This is why long-time desktop users hit "sync failed" while recently-logged-in mobile users (UUID tokens) were fine.

- api-server/middlewares/auth.ts: validate UUID shape before the lookup so bad tokens degrade to a clean 401 instead of a 500.
- scent-cast/WardrobeContext.tsx: on 401 from /api/wardrobe, sign out the dead token and reopen the auth modal ("Session Expired") instead of looping on a generic "Synchronization Error".

Verified live: non-UUID token -> 500, valid-shaped-but-unknown UUID -> 401, confirming the cast was the crash.

author: hsukenooi
body:
## Summary

A June 2026 qualitycomix seller scan exposed three grader failures. This ships **Phase 1** of the BUI-51 plan, which fixes all three and — crucially — makes a grade's *confidence* actually move the bid downstream.

Before: printed creator credits on an early-'90s cover were read as handwritten signatures and capped the grade at 9.0; a 2-photo listing returned a point-precise grade that FMV then bid on as if it were a 6-photo assessment; and every comic burned 3 grader agents regardless of value. After: printed elements never cap, grade confidence is derived from photo *coverage* and haircuts the bid when thin, and cheap unambiguous lots use a single grader.

| Front | Change | Closes |
|---|---|---|
| **Accuracy** | Print-layer rule — printed credits / facsimile signatures / barcodes / price boxes are never defects (grounded in CGC's defect taxonomy: *Writing* / *Name Written on Cover* are post-print substance defects; printed elements aren't in the taxonomy). Only post-print marks cap; **ambiguous → no cap** (the failure was false positives). | #1 in the ticket |
| **Confidence** | Grade confidence now derives from which photo *views* are present, not image count. Emits a confidence level + grade range; a 2-cover-photo lot caps at MEDIUM-LOW. It rides the `comic-fmv --batch` envelope and **haircuts the bid cap** (`0.80 → 0.70 / 0.60`) by the more conservative of grade-confidence and comp-confidence — so a thinly-photographed comic bids lower. | #2 |
| **Efficiency** | Value-gated fan-out — 1 grader first, escalate to a 3-grader panel only on auction value ≥ threshold or a boundary-ambiguous grade. Targets the ~60% agent cut. | #3 |

## Why the confidence haircut is the load-bearing piece

The actual BUI-51 #2 bug wasn't that the grader returned point grades — it's that the confidence *died in the grader's text output*. A 2-photo guess and a 6-photo assessment bid identically. The fix lives in the handoff: the grader emits `grade_confidence`, it threads through `/comic:buy`'s working list into the `comic-fmv` CLI, and the CLI lowers the `0.80 × fmv_high` multiplier when confidence is low.

```
grade.md (confidence from coverage)
  → working-list JSON {grade, grade_confidence}
    → comic-fmv --batch
      → max_bid = clean_round( min(grade_conf, fmv_conf) → factor × fmv_high )
```

## Key decisions

- **Haircut lives in the `comic-fmv` CLI** (`apps/fmv`), not skill prose — that's where the bid cap is actually computed. A prose-only change would have left the math untouched.
- **Two confidence axes stay separate.** `fmv_confidence` (comp-pool quality) and `grade_confidence` (photo coverage) are orthogonal; the haircut takes the **more conservative** of the two rather than collapsing them into one number.
- **Confidence is not persisted to the DB** (no new column) — it stays in the handoff envelope. The cache-reuse path still applies the haircut at *read* time, so a cache hit on a freshly low-confidence grade doesn't silently bid at full 80%.
- **Untrusted input is hardened.** `grade_confidence` is LLM-authored via JSON; a non-string, blank, or typo'd value neither crashes nor fails open — blank is treated as absent, and an unrecognized value leans conservative (LOW).
- **Back-compat:** absent `grade_confidence` (seller-stated grades, manual runs) → unchanged 80% bid.

## Test plan

- `apps/fmv` suite: **84 passing** (added `bid_factor`, `compute_fmv` haircut, cached-path haircut, and runner-threading tests covering both-high / conservative-min / MEDIUM-no-haircut / non-string / blank / unknown-label / back-compat).
- Skill-prose units (`grade.md`, `buy.md`, `fmv.md`, `snipe-add.md`) verified by output-format/contract inspection — there is no automated harness for skill markdown.
- Tier-1 code review ran (3 parallel finders); its findings were fixed in this branch: hardened untrusted `grade_confidence`, preserved MEDIUM-LOW end-to-end (so 2-photo lots haircut at the intended 0.70), closed the cache-reuse gap, and tightened weak/tautological tests.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

No production/runtime deploy — these are local CLIs (`apps/fmv`) plus Claude Code skill prose. Validate by:
1. Re-run `/comic:grade` on the qualitycomix X-Men #24 (1993) listing → confirm **no signature cap** and no grade reduction from the printed credits.
2. Run `comic-fmv --batch` with a row carrying `grade_confidence: "low"` → confirm `max_bid ≈ 0.60 × fmv_high` and a `bid_haircut=…` note in the row's `fmv_notes`.

No rollback infra needed; revert the branch if the haircut over-suppresses bids in practice.

## Follow-up (deferred)

Phase 2 of the plan (`docs/plans/2026-06-03-001-feat-comic-grader-accuracy-efficiency-plan.md`, left `status: active`) holds the stretch set, not executed here: seller-grade-as-prior, structured defect extraction, decision-sensitivity gating, batch-cheap-lots, and a triage pre-pass.

Linear: BUI-51.

body:
### Motivation

- Provide a reliable visual representation of the final landing by rendering the final HTML in a headless browser and sending screenshots to the OpenAI Responses API instead of sending raw image URLs extracted from HTML.
- Avoid failures caused by non-image URLs (tracking pixels / scripts) and improve the commercial quality gate by evaluating the real rendered experience.

### Description

- Added a `QualityReviewScreenshotService` and a `PlaywrightQualityReviewScreenshotService` that launches Chromium via Playwright, renders `htmlGeraLanding` (with fallback to `landingPageHtml`) in desktop and mobile viewports, captures full-page JPEG screenshots and uploads them via `FrameworkImageStorageClient` for public URLs.
- Switched the prompt pipeline to use rendered screenshots: `QualityReviewPromptBuilder` now requests screenshots from `QualityReviewScreenshotService`, injects `renderedLandingScreenshots` into the prompt context and includes those URLs as `input_image` entries in the Responses API request.
- Replaced previous image-URL-extraction logic in `QualityReviewBackendClient` with `resolveLandingHtml(...)` so the backend exposes final HTML to be rendered; added logging and safer JSON serialization handling.
- Exposed new properties `qualityreview.worker.chromium-executable-path` and `qualityreview.worker.screenshot-timeout` via `QualityReviewWorkerProperties` with sane defaults, and registered the screenshot service bean in `QualityReviewWorkerConfiguration`.
- Updated runtime image in the `ai-worker/Dockerfile` to `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright/java:v1.49.0-jammy` and added `com.microsoft.playwright:playwright:1.49.0` to `pom.xml` so Chromium is available at runtime.
- Added unit tests `QualityReviewBackendClientTest` and `QualityReviewPromptBuilderTest`, updated prompt template and docs to describe the screenshot-based approach and recorded the rationale and regressions fixed.

### Testing

- Ran new unit tests `QualityReviewBackendClientTest` and `QualityReviewPromptBuilderTest`, and both tests passed.
- Ran module unit test suite for `ai-worker` locally and no regressions were observed in the modified area.

## Summary

- **`ExtractFlows`** (`internal/codegraph/flows.go`): bounded DFS over the in-memory `cg` after `injectCommunities` + `computeSymbolPageRank` — no AGE round-trips. Entry-points = HANDLES targets (route handlers) ∪ zero-caller exported symbols. Chains stay within one Louvain community, named `<entry> → <dominant-leaf>` (PageRank-weighted endpoints), priority = max PR along chain, capped at `flowsMax=50`.
- **`code_flows` table** (`internal/codegraph/store_flows.go`, ADR-001): plain relational with nullable `vector(768)` column for future `FLOWS_IN_SEARCH`. Delete-then-insert reconcile on every `IndexRepo` pass. `CopyFrom` + `VALUES` fallback.
- **`list_flows` MCP tool** (`cmd/go-code/tool_list_flows.go`): DB-gated (`graphStore==nil` → disabled), mirrors `registerOrphanSweep` pattern exactly. Input `{repo}`, output flows sorted by priority.

- **Wired into `IndexRepo`** (`internal/codegraph/index.go`): called after `injectCommunities`, reuses `computeSymbolPageRank` result. `buildCrossLanguageData` hoisted before flow extraction so HANDLES targets are available. Non-fatal: logs + bumps counter on DB write failure.

- `FLOWS_IN_SEARCH` retrieval signal (column ships nullable, search integration flag does NOT — `semantic_search` output byte-identical to de3a099)
- `explore` digest surface

- `go test ./internal/codegraph/ ./cmd/go-code/`: ok (127s full suite)
- `golangci-lint run ./internal/codegraph/ ./cmd/go-code/`: 0 new issues in changed files (pre-existing issues unrelated to this PR)

## Tests
9 `ExtractFlows` unit tests + 4 `tool_list_flows` format tests.

**Falsification evidence**: reverting `ExtractFlows` (or the HANDLES entry-point detection) causes `TestExtractFlows_EntryPointFromHANDLES` and `TestExtractFlows_EntryPointFromZeroCaller` to fail with "no flows" immediately. Reverting `flowsMax` cap breaks `TestExtractFlows_FlowsMaxCap`. All tests confirmed RED before implementation.

|---|---|---|
| `computeSymbolPageRank` in IndexRepo | `index.go:130` (called with root+allSymbols+cg) | ✓ |
| `injectCommunities` before flow extraction | `index.go:120→130` ordering preserved | ✓ |
| `buildCrossLanguageData` for HANDLES targets | hoisted to `index.go:132`, reused for main insert | ✓ |
| `CallChainNode` DFS pattern | DFS reimplemented as `dfsCollectChain` over raw `*parser.Symbol` (simpler, no XML overhead) | adapted |

author: scienceisneato
body:
Two follow-ups from the #244/#245 review, plus one bundled security pin needed to keep scour green.

## 1. Shared string-aware JSONC parser

The #245 review surfaced three escalating bugs in an ad-hoc pyright-config comment stripper (block comments, then string-boundary corruption, then logic). The same fragile regex approach also lived in the knip-config reader. New `slopmop/utils/jsonc.py` provides one hardened, **string-aware** `strip_jsonc`/`loads_jsonc` (handles `//`, `/* */`, trailing commas; never touches contents of quoted strings like `"src/**"` or `"http://x"`). Wired into both the pyright (`type_checking.py`) and knip (`dead_code.py`) readers; removed the now-unused `re` imports.

> Out of scope: `dart/bogus_tests.py` has a `_strip_comments` too, but it operates on **Dart source**, not JSON — a JSON-oriented util would be wrong there, so it's left alone.

## 2. Barnacles always get labeled

`#244` and `#245` came in **unlabeled**. Root cause: when a repo lacks the `barnacle` label, the filer silently dropped the label and filed the issue without it — exactly how friction reports become invisible to `--label barnacle` triage. The filer now **creates the label and retries with it**, only filing without as a last resort (and warning loudly when it does).

## 3. (bundled) pyjwt security pin

pip-audit flagged `pyjwt 2.12.1` (transitive via semgrep/mcp) for PYSEC-2026-175/177/179 — a pre-existing, advisory-driven `dependency-risk` failure unrelated to the above, but it blocks the shared scour gate. Pinned `pyjwt>=2.13.0` the same way the neighboring transitive deps (python-multipart, starlette) are handled.

Closes #244
Closes #245

## Test plan

- [x] `sm scour` clean (18 passed, 1 pre-existing non-blocking config-debt warning)
- [x] New `tests/unit/test_jsonc.py` covers comment/trailing-comma stripping and string-boundary preservation (the exact glob case that broke the regex)
- [x] Barnacle tests updated: label-create-and-retry path, plus last-resort warning path
- [ ] CI green

> Note: #244 and #245 are already closed (their fixes merged in #246/#247); the `Closes` keywords here are belt-and-suspenders for the label/follow-up work and harmless if already closed.

## Summary

Started as "add Predate," became a proper closure of the D1 divergence and a clean decomposition of the fight mechanic. Four commits, building on each other:

1. **`d990983` — doc corrections.** Two docs (`reference/html-proto/CLAUDE.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`) wrongly claimed static lords grant stats but *not* keywords. They do — via `applyStaticKeywordGrants` (6 lord cards). Fixed.

2. **`387ed9b` (v2.0.77) — Predate + the D1 hybrid it forces.** New card **Predate** ({1}{G} Sorcery): *"Target creature you control gets +1/+1 until end of turn, then it fights target creature an opponent controls."* The pump-then-fight forces the **D1 live-read hybrid** (DIVERGENCE §3.6): a `{from:'target_*'}` expression reads **live** state while the target is on the battlefield (so the pump counts in the fight) and falls back to the **last-known-info snapshot** once it has left its zone (Swords/Exorcist: exile, then gain life = its power). Closes D1 on the proto side. Also pinned the previously-untested static-lord keyword grant.

3. **`1f29841` (v2.0.78) — decompose `fight_target` → `fight`.** Separated the fight mechanic from the fighter-selection policy.

4. **`144b7bc` (v2.0.79) — symmetric operands + `target_slots`-authoritative enumeration.** `fight` is now a clean two-operand primitive — `operands: [{slot}|{select}, ...]`, both combatants read from `ctx.allTargets`, no `fighter`/`target_slot`. Root cause of the earlier asymmetry: the AI enumeration path derived target slots from effects, while the UI/probe path already read `card.target_slots`. Made `validTargetsBySlot` / `isLegalAction` / `getLegalActions` treat `card.target_slots` as authoritative — behavior-identical for every existing multi-target card. This unblocked **Prey Upon** ({G} Sorcery, *"target creature you control fights target creature an opponent controls"*), a fight-only two-target card that was impossible to author before.

## Notable bug fixed

v2.0.77/78 Predate was **AI-uncastable** — a targeted cast scores purely through `scoreMultiTargetSpell`, which returned 0 for a slot-only card (no `e.target`/`card.target`), so the `≤0 → don't cast` gate dropped it. The end-to-end test had masked it by casting Predate directly. New `scoreFightExchange` scores the exchange off operands; the AI now casts Predate/Prey Upon when favorable and declines bad trades (verified via `AI.decide`).

## Card text

Renders "<A> fights <B>" from operands, picking the pronoun automatically:
- Predate → "…then **it** fights target creature an opponent controls."
- Prey Upon → "**Target creature you control** fights target creature an opponent controls."
- Beast's Fury → "**Your strongest creature** fights target creature an opponent controls."

author: josh-cpm
body:
## What

Counts WhisperFree active installs **server-side**, with no in-app telemetry, by observing Sparkle's daily poll of `/appcast.xml`.

- **`netlify/edge-functions/appcast.js`** — intercepts `/appcast.xml`, records one anonymized ping, then serves the unchanged static feed via `context.next()`. Sparkle sees an identical response; the release pipeline is untouched.
- **`netlify/functions/stats.mjs`** — token-protected `/stats` JSON readout (current-month active installs + per-month history).
- Adds `@netlify/blobs` for storage (auto-provisioned by Netlify).

## Privacy design

- Raw IP is **never stored** — we store `SHA-256(INSTALL_SALT : YYYY-MM : ip)`.
- `INSTALL_SALT` is a server-side secret, so the hash can't be reversed or tested against a known IP.
- The period is the calendar month, so an install hashes to the same value **within** a month (→ monthly-unique "active installs") but is **uncorrelatable across** months.
- One tiny idempotent Blobs key per unique install (`${period}/${hash}`); no read-modify-write races, bounded growth.

## Metric

Monthly-unique installs = "active installs." Honest privacy/accuracy tradeoff: daily counts undercount (machines sleep), naive multi-day counts double-count. Counts begin accumulating on deploy (no historical backfill).

## Required env vars (set in Netlify, all contexts)

- `INSTALL_SALT` — secret salt for hashing
- `STATS_TOKEN` — shared secret to read `/stats`

## Read the number

```sh
curl "https://whisperfree.com/stats?token=$STATS_TOKEN"
```

## Verification

- Astro build passes on Node 22.
- Both functions pass `node --check`.

author: sebastionoss
body:
## Vulnerability Summary

The `verifyRequestSignature` function in `app.js` (line 90) is used as the `verify` callback for Express's `body-parser` JSON middleware. This callback is designed to reject invalid requests by **throwing an error** — that's the only mechanism body-parser provides for the `verify` callback to abort request processing.

When the `x-hub-signature-256` header is present but invalid, the function correctly throws. However, when the header is **missing entirely**, the function only calls `console.warn()` and returns normally. Because body-parser treats a non-throwing `verify` callback as success, the request proceeds through to the `POST /webhook` handler with an unsigned, potentially forged payload.

This is **CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature**. The signature check exists but is trivially bypassed by omitting the signature header altogether.

## Affected Code

- **File:** `app.js`
- **Function:** `verifyRequestSignature` (line 90)
- **Middleware binding:** `app.use(json({ verify: verifyRequestSignature }))` (line 29)
- **Affected endpoint:** `POST /webhook` (line 45)

## Fix Description

Replace `console.warn()` with `throw new Error()` in the `!signature` branch. This is a one-line change that makes the missing-header case consistent with the invalid-signature case — both now throw, causing body-parser to reject the request with a 403.

This matches the documented behavior of Express body-parser's `verify` option: "The verify function can be used to abort parsing by throwing an error."

## Proof of Concept

An attacker can send forged webhook payloads without any signature header. On the **unfixed** code:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/webhook \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"object":"whatsapp_business_account","entry":[{"id":"123","changes":[{"value":{"messaging_product":"whatsapp","metadata":{"display_phone_number":"15551234567","phone_number_id":"123456"},"messages":[{"from":"15559876543","id":"wamid.test","timestamp":"1234567890","text":{"body":"forged message"},"type":"text"}]},"field":"messages"}]}]}'
```

On the current `main` branch, this request is accepted (HTTP 200) and the forged message is processed by the webhook handler. The server logs a warning but does not reject the request. With this fix applied, the same request returns HTTP 403 because body-parser's verify callback throws before the route handler executes.

## Testing

- Verified that requests **without** `x-hub-signature-256` are rejected (403) after the fix
- Verified that requests **with a valid** `x-hub-signature-256` are accepted (200) as before
- Verified that requests **with an invalid** signature continue to be rejected (403)

## Adversarial Review

Before submitting, we considered whether any other middleware or framework-level protection might prevent exploitation. There is none — Express does not enforce webhook signatures, and the `verify` callback in body-parser is the sole gating mechanism. The only preconditions are network access to the webhook endpoint and knowledge of the URL path (`/webhook`), both of which are standard for any deployed webhook receiver. The `console.warn` call provides no security protection; it is purely informational logging that does not affect request processing.

Closes #35

## What

Enable drag-and-drop file moves from the right-hand listing pane onto folders in the left file tree.

The backend (`/api/move`) and the DnD helpers (`attachMcDrag` / `attachMcDrop` / `mcMove`) already existed and were wired into the **left tree** — but the **right-pane listing rows were not draggable**, so there was no way to start a drag from the listing. This PR closes that gap:

- Document rows in the listing are now `draggable` and can be dropped onto any tree folder (or onto a subfolder row).
- Subfolder rows in the listing are both draggable **and** valid drop targets.
- `mcMove` now also optimistically expands the destination in the main sidebar tree, so a dropped item lands somewhere already visible before the SSE reindex arrives.

No new endpoint or move logic — all safety checks are reused.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A file in the right pane can be dragged.
- [x] Valid drop targets (folder nodes in the tree) highlight on drag-over — `mc-drop-ok` / `mc-drop-bad` via existing `attachMcDrop`.
- [x] Dropping on a folder moves the item (persisted via `/api/move`).
- [x] The right pane and tree refresh — SSE/chokidar `index-changed` + optimistic expand.
- [x] Dropping a folder into itself or a descendant is prevented (client `mcDropAcceptable` + server guard).
- [x] No-op drops (onto current parent) handled gracefully (`{ ok: true, unchanged: true }`).
- [x] A failed move surfaces an error and leaves the item in place (`uiAlert` + server leaves source untouched on collision).

## Test

Ran the real server against a throwaway workspace (`node serve.js -p <tmp>`):

**Backend `/api/move` (curl):**
- happy-path file move → `ok`, file present at destination on disk
- no-op onto own parent → `{ ok: true, unchanged: true }`
- folder into itself / descendant → `cannot move a folder into itself`
- name collision → `409 already exists`, source left in place
- nonexistent / missing source → `source not found` / `missing srcPath`
- valid folder move → `ok`, folder relocated on disk

**Client wiring (headless Chromium / Playwright):**
- Right-pane folder rows and doc rows render with `draggable="true"`.
- Synthetic `dragstart`(listing doc row) → `dragover`/`drop`(tree folder) fired `/api/move` with the correct `{ srcPath, destFolder }`.
- The targeted file actually moved on disk through the live endpoint.
- No console errors during render or drop.

`:id` accepts either an opaque oid or a foreign_id scoped to the `namespace` query param, via a new `resolve_for_read` helper in `BaseController`. The `granted_*`/`sync_*` assembly moved from `Proxy` to `Principal` (its natural home) with `Proxy` delegating, leaving `Proxy#config_hash` unchanged.

author: psychollama
body:
## TL;DR

Integrates the seven Renovate PRs that had **green CI** (skipping the three that were red), then fixes two latent pnpm-config issues the work surfaced. Each dependency bump is pinned to the exact version its passing Renovate PR tested (lockfile-only, ranges untouched). Full `pnpm check` is green (30/30) on the refreshed toolchain.

## Dependency bumps (passing Renovate PRs)

| Renovate | Update |
|---|---|
| #245 | `@iconify/json` → 2.2.480 |
| #257 | `knip` → 6.14.2 |
| #261 | `turbo` → 2.9.16 |
| #256 | storybook monorepo → 10.4.1 (storybook-solidjs-vite held at 10.0.12) |
| #252 | vitest monorepo → 4.1.7 |
| #250 | typescript-eslint monorepo → 8.60.0 |

Skipped (red CI): #259 tinyexec, #253 storybook-solidjs-vite 10.1.1, #25 vite v8.

Each was applied by pinning the exact PR-tested version into the lockfile and leaving the manifest range floors as Renovate does — a plain `pnpm update` drifted past the tested versions (e.g. knip → 6.15.0) and would have pulled the red storybook-solidjs-vite 10.1.1.

## pnpm / flake fixes (surfaced by the work)

- **Migrate `pnpm.overrides` → `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.** pnpm 11.4 stopped reading the `pnpm` field in `package.json`, so the override pinning framework singletons to the catalog had gone inert on `main` — a duplicate `vite@8.0.11` had crept in via `@vanilla-extract/integration`. Moving it to the top-level `overrides:` key re-applies it and collapses vite back to a single 7.3.3.
- **Update `nixpkgs`** (2026-05-07 → 06-01): pnpm 10.33.2 → 11.4.0, nodejs → 24.15.0.
- **Let the flake own pnpm.** `manage-package-manager-versions` (on by default) made the `packageManager` field self-upgrade pnpm away from the nix binary. Turbo *requires* the field (and reads its major to pick the pnpm9 lockfile parser), so it can't be removed — instead `managePackageManagerVersions: false` + pin to the flake's version. The nix-provided pnpm is now used verbatim; comments in `flake.nix` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` flag the sync requirement.

## Pros

- Branch carries only green-CI dependency versions, pinned to exactly what was tested.
- Fixes a silent regression (duplicate vite) and makes the flake the real source of truth for pnpm.
- Clean, bisectable history: one commit per concern.

## Cons / known tradeoffs

- The re-activated `vite` override forces vanilla-extract's compiler (`vite-node@6.0.0`, hard-deps `vite ^8`) down to 7.3.3. The `bundle` task and all tests pass, but it's technically an unsupported combo. Chosen deliberately over reintroducing a second vite copy. (Flagged by codex; accepted.)
- `packageManager` now pins a concrete pnpm version that will drift from `nixpkgs` over time; with version management disabled it's inert for pnpm and only turbo reads the major, so drift is harmless but the value can look stale.

## Recommended follow-ups

- Add a Renovate ignore rule for the `packageManager` field — its bump PRs (e.g. #249) are now no-ops since the flake owns the version.
- Revisit the `vite` override when the app can move to vite 8 (Renovate #25), which would let vanilla-extract's compiler return to a supported vite.

body:
## Why

Debugging the operator brain needs a second observability plane. `/logs` (Loki) catches requests *rejected before the graph runs* (auth, Zod 400 like `modelRef field is required`); it is **blind to graphs that run but answer wrong** — wrong tool, empty output, `status:"error"` aborts, or "the repo tools are failing (no git)". Those live only in Langfuse, which had no skill and no MCP server.

## What

- **`.claude/commands/traces.md`** — `/traces` skill, parallel to `/logs`. Covers the logs-vs-traces split, the trace/observation/session data model, top-down collection recipe, and a **capability-gap** discipline (a `success` trace that only ever called `knowledge_search` is a missing-adapter finding, not a pass).
- **`scripts/langfuse-query.sh`** — MCP-less curl reader, the `loki-query.sh` counterpart. Greps `LANGFUSE_*` from `.env.cogni` (avoids the `<placeholder>` sourcing trap), Basic-auths the Public API.
- **`logs.md`** — one cross-reference pointer to `/traces`.

## Gotcha captured

The Cogni Langfuse project lives on the **US** region (`https://us.cloud.langfuse.com`). The EU host (`cloud.langfuse.com`, the stale "Default" in `infra/secrets-catalog.yaml`) rejects the same keys with `Invalid credentials. Confirm that you've configured the correct host.` The script defaults to US.

## Verification

`scripts/langfuse-query.sh '/api/public/traces?limit=3&...'` returns live prod traces (smoke-tested green). Docs/skill-only change — no app code touched.

body:
## Summary

Implements E3 from the product roadmap: post-tax income estimate alongside the standard 4% SWR, giving FIRE-stage users a realistic view of what they can actually spend after capital gains tax.

**Key insight:** A ₹1Cr corpus at 4% SWR generates ₹4L/year gross. After LTCG/STCG/debt tax under India Budget 2024 rules, the net can be closer to ₹3–3.2L. This feature makes that gap visible.

---

## What's new

### `src/utils/taxCalculator.ts` (new file)
Pure calculation module — no React, no side effects, fully unit-tested:
- **`calcWithdrawalTax(annualGross, taxParams) → TaxBreakdown`**  
  Splits annual withdrawal into equity LTCG / STCG / debt, applies India Budget 2024:  
  LTCG 12.5% above ₹1.25L annual exemption · STCG 20% · Debt at 30% slab · 4% cess.  
  Conservative assumption: full withdrawal treated as capital gains (overestimates tax slightly, appropriate for large mature portfolios where basis ≪ current value).
- **`grossForNetWithdrawal(targetNet, taxParams)`** — binary-search inverse: how much gross to withdraw to net a target amount
- **`DEFAULT_TAX_PARAMS`** — India Budget 2024 defaults (12.5 / 20 / 30 / 4%, 80/70 equity split, ₹1.25L exemption)

### `src/types/index.ts`
- New `TaxParams` interface (7 fields)
- `Goal.taxParams?: TaxParams` — absent means tax section is hidden; set to enable

### GoalEditor — Tax settings section
New "Tax-aware withdrawal" collapsible toggle for FIRE goals:
- Checkbox to enable post-tax display
- 6 editable fields pre-filled with Budget 2024 defaults: Equity %, LTCG % of equity, LTCG rate, STCG rate, Debt rate, LTCG exemption amount
- Settings saved on the Goal object (persisted in IndexedDB)

### FIREDashboard — Two new UI elements
1. **After-tax sub-line on SWR stat** — when `taxParams` set, shows net monthly income and effective tax rate inline: `₹2.9L net · 23.4% tax`
2. **"Tax impact" panel** — button alongside "What if?"; opens a line-by-line breakdown:
   - Equity LTCG gains → tax (with exemption callout)
   - Equity STCG gains → tax
   - Debt gains → tax
   - Cess
   - Total tax + net annual and monthly income
   - Footer note explaining conservative assumption and how to adjust rates
   - Panels are mutually exclusive (opening one closes the other)
   - Resets to closed when goal switches

---

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm run test` — 182 tests, all passing
- [ ] `npm run build` — TypeScript clean
- [ ] **Create a FIRE goal** → edit → expand "Tax-aware withdrawal" → enable checkbox → verify 6 fields appear with Budget 2024 defaults → save
- [ ] **FIRE dashboard** → SWR stat shows "₹X net · Y% tax" sub-line
- [ ] **"Tax impact" button** → opens breakdown panel with correct line items
- [ ] **Check LTCG exemption logic**: for small corpus where LTCG gains < ₹1.25L, LTCG tax line shows ₹0
- [ ] **Mutual exclusion**: opening "Tax impact" while "What if?" is open closes the scenario panel and vice versa
- [ ] **Goal without taxParams** → no "Tax impact" button shown, SWR stat shows original "Passive income / mo" sub-line

## Summary

Largest end-user-visible PR of the [2026-06-03 feeder-family alignment audit](https://github.com/HiroAlleyCat) sweep. Brings Heimdall to feature parity with Muninn and wigle-to-wdgwars for the install / schedule / daily-run flow, and aligns the flag names so muscle memory transfers across the family.

**PR 4 of 4** in the sweep.

## Added

- **Schedule installer**: `--schedule` / `--unschedule` / `--schedule-csv PATH` / `--schedule-time HH:MM` / `--schedule-dry-run`. Installs the right artifact per OS:
  - Linux + systemd → user systemd timer
  - macOS / Linux without systemd → user crontab
  - Windows → schtasks
  Every artifact carries a `# managed-by-heimdall` marker for clean removal. **The API key is never baked into the unit file** — saved-on-disk key is read at run-time.
- **Canonical flag names** matching Muninn + wigle: `--key` (was `--api-key`) and `--api-url` (was `--endpoint`).
- `scripts/smoke.sh` — pre-release smoke (README linter + AST/import + offline tests + `--version` / `--help` + Linux/systemd unit-write roundtrip + no-key-leak assertion).
- `scripts/check_readme_examples.py` — README linter ported from Muninn / wigle, auto-detects entrypoint script.
- `tests/test_scheduler.py` — 17 new tests covering pure renderers + HH:MM validation + mechanism selector + no-credential-leak assertions (full suite is now 28 tests).
- README `## Running on a schedule` section with per-OS mechanism table.
- README `## Troubleshooting` section.

## Changed

- `_prompt_yes_no` emits an explicit newline after consuming a piped-stdin answer. Interactive TTY gets one from the terminal; piped input doesn't, and would otherwise glue the next section header onto the prompt line.
- `setup.sh` / `run.sh` / `update.sh` now `[ -t 0 ]`-gate the trailing `Press any key to close...` so piped / non-TTY invocations exit cleanly.
- README code-block examples rewritten from `python3 heimdall.py ...` to `./run.sh ...` (the venv-aware shim). Two intentional stdlib-only bootstrap examples annotated `# direct invocation` to keep the linter quiet.

## Deprecated

- `--api-key` → use `--key`. Old name still works and now emits a one-line deprecation note on stderr. **Removed in v0.4**.
- `--endpoint` → use `--api-url`. Same treatment.

## Not changed (out of audit scope)

- gungnir extraction: Heimdall is still stdlib + inlined HMAC. The earlier `v0.2-gungnir` extraction branch never landed on main. Architectural refactor, not alignment work — filed as a tracked note for a separate session.

## Test plan

- [x] \`HEIMDALL_TEST_ALLOW_LIVE_KEY=1 python3 -m unittest discover tests/\` — 28 tests pass.
- [x] \`bash scripts/smoke.sh\` — all 5 sections green on Windows (Git Bash, systemd section skipped).
- [x] Deprecation alias smoke: \`./heimdall.py --no-version-check --api-key X --whoami\` emits the warning + still hits `/api/me`.
- [x] Render purity confirmed: `render_systemd_units` / `render_cron_line` / `render_schtasks_create` never include the API key value in their output.
- [ ] CI workflow passes.
- [ ] Manual end-to-end Linux systemd install on a test host (deferred to a separate verification turn — needs a real systemd box).

## Migration notes for users

The old flag names keep working through v0.3.x. To silence the deprecation note before v0.4:

```bash
# Before
./run.sh my.csv --api-key X --endpoint http://localhost/api/
# After
./run.sh my.csv --key X --api-url http://localhost/api/
```

author: romanbabenkorostov-ux
body:
## Что чинит

У пользователя в свежем клоне:

```
uvicorn backend.app.main:app --reload --port 8000
...
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'backend'
```

И параллельно: `http.server` на `/` отдаёт листинг папки, что выглядит как «пустой сайт».

## Корневая причина

1. **`ModuleNotFoundError 'backend'`**: uvicorn запускается из `Scripts/`-папки venv. Текущий каталог НЕ попадает в `sys.path`. С `--reload` это ещё хуже — reloader-подпроцесс не наследует никаких `sys.path`-модификаций, сделанных родительским процессом.
2. **Чужой venv**: пользователь активировал `E:\Code\!util\сoder_exif\backend\venv` — там пакеты от другого проекта.
3. **`http.server` показывает листинг**: пользователь зашёл на `http://localhost:8001/`, нужно `/viewer/index.html`.

## Решение

### `serve.py` (новый, в корне репо)

Foolproof launcher:
- Выставляет `PYTHONPATH=<repo_root>` через `os.environ` — это **переживает** `--reload` subprocess (uvicorn передаёт env в reloader).
- Дублирует sys.path для текущего процесса.
- Детектит чужой venv (`VIRTUAL_ENV` не внутри корня репо) → WARNING с копипаст-инструкцией.
- Перехватывает `ImportError uvicorn` → печатает шаги установки.
- CLI: `--host --port --no-reload --log-level`.

Эквивалент: `uvicorn --app-dir . backend.app.main:app --reload`.

### Использование

```powershell
python serve.py                      # 127.0.0.1:8000, reload включён
python serve.py --port 9000          # кастомный порт
python serve.py --no-reload          # без watcher
python serve.py --host 0.0.0.0       # все интерфейсы
```

### Документация

В `obsidian/UserGuide/clone-and-run.md`:
- Шаг 4: акцент «venv ВНУТРИ корня клона» + проверка `where python` / `which python`.
- Шаг 6: `python serve.py` как рекомендуемый способ; альтернатива `uvicorn --app-dir .`; объяснение почему голый `uvicorn backend.app.main:app` падает.
- Шаг 7: акцент «откройте `/viewer/index.html`, а не `/`».
- Troubleshooting: 3 новые секции — про `ModuleNotFoundError 'backend'`, про чужой venv, про листинг `http.server`.

## Test plan

- [x] **Свежий клон smoke**: `cp` всё репо в `/tmp/fresh-clone`, `python serve.py --no-reload --port 8765` → `GET / = 200`, `GET /openapi.json = 200`, 6 paths, `title="Ekcelo Orchestrator"`.
- [x] **Reload-режим smoke** (та же ошибка, что у пользователя): `python serve.py --port 8766` → `GET / = 200`. Не падает.
- [x] **78/78 pass** (68 base + 10 launcher tests): foreign venv detection, sys.path mutations, argparse, `subprocess: python serve.py --help`.
- [x] Никаких изменений в logic-коде; serve.py — отдельный launcher.

## Связи

- backend layout: `backend/app/` (PR #95, merged)
- инструкция: `obsidian/UserGuide/clone-and-run.md` (PR #94, merged)

author: nathanlmeyers
body:
A native macOS **menu-bar app** for curating Spotify as you listen: see the current song, **Add** it to a target playlist or **Remove** it from the one you're listening to, and a **Discovery mode** that holds playback at the end of each track so you can triage new releases.

## What's included
**Phase 1 — Core**
- Menu-bar-only app (SwiftUI hosted in AppKit), generated via XcodeGen.
- Local playback read/control via a ScriptingBridge shim to the Spotify desktop app (no Premium); Spotify **Web API** (OAuth 2.0 + PKCE, tokens in Keychain) for playlist edits.
- `MusicProvider` abstraction (`SpotifyProvider` first impl) so Apple Music etc. can be added later.
- Now-playing panel: artwork, seek scrubber, transport + shuffle, **Add/Remove** with gray-out states + tooltips; settings target picker (editable-only), move-on-add, dup-prevention, edge-content handling.

**Phase 2 — Discovery mode**
- Computed precise-pause hold (pauses ~0.8s before a track's natural end; crossfade/slip fallback), combinable alerts (auto-open panel / icon shade / sound), auto-skip rules (already-in-target, already-reviewed) with loop protection.

**Live fixes & polish (this session's verification)**
- **Fixed 403 on add/remove/read-items**: Spotify removed `/playlists/{id}/tracks` in Feb 2026 — migrated to the new `/playlists/{id}/items` endpoints.
- Discovery now reliably holds the **ending** song (lead 0.30s → 0.8s).
- **Featured artists** shown on the display (full Web API artist list).
- Discovery-themed **menu-bar icon** (magnifier + music note) that shades solid while a song is held.
- Now-playing panel **hugs the menu bar** (replaced the arrow popover with a tight borderless panel).
- File-based `DebugLog` + persistent error status for diagnosability.

## Verified
- Builds clean (Swift 6.2 / Xcode 26); 10/10 unit tests pass (URI classification, editability, auto-skip order, loop protection).
- Live: login (PKCE), Add/Remove against owned playlists, source detection, discovery hold + alerts.

## Setup note
Requires a personal Spotify Developer app Client ID in a gitignored `Secrets.xcconfig` (redirect URI `spotifymenubar://callback`). See `README.md`. Dev-mode apps can read/modify only the user's own/collaborative playlists.

## Follow-ups (tracked as issues)
- Apple Music + multi-provider support (#1)
- Public distribution: notarization + Spotify quota (#2)

This **completes batch-1 distillation** — every chapter-loop-dispatchable book is now in masters.json.

## #350 OCR audit gate satisfied

The chapter-loop's substring-fidelity check IS the OCR-quality verifier. All 6 vols produced fidelity-validated quotes (where prose existed). Vol-5 was the only volume with substantive content loss — worker honestly flagged real method content (GB Chord Transitions Ch6, augmented-arpeggio rules Ch9) absent from systems-draft due to OCR artifacts (`'7lux'` for `'flux'`, `'<initely'` for `'finitely'`, multi-column joins). Curator note: chs 5 / 6 / 9 / 11 candidates for re-OCR or character-normalized re-extraction once #298 lands.

## CRITICAL pipeline finding (separate ticket worth)

vol-6 worker discovered the bridge's **s4-statement.request.json builder pulled vol-7 inputs into the vol-6 run's s4-statement request body**. The cross-run contamination class previously observed on s2-toc requests (galbraith→Aebersold #373, bertoncini→mixed #374, laukens-patterns→Felts #378) **also affects s4-statement** for concurrent siblings.

Worker mitigation: grounded the LLM call directly on the correct on-disk vol-6 sources, ignoring the corrupted request user_prompt. The resulting STATEMENT.md cites only vol-6 content (Giant Lines, Flux & Reflux, GB Chord Transitions, Ending Note Rule, etc.) and matches the systems-draft exactly.

**Spot-check before bundle**: I verified all 6 benson STATEMENT H1 titles match the expected work_id:
- vol-2 → "The George Benson Method, Vol. 2 (Advanced Harmony)"
- vol-3 → "Vol 3 Technique & Arpeggios"
- vol-4 → "The George Benson Method, Vol. 4 (Approach Tones, Dorian, Mixolydian & Harmonic Minor World)"

- vol-6 → "The Secret of the Giant Lines" (worker-mitigated; correct content)
- vol-7 → "The George Benson Method, Vol. 7 (Ultimate Advanced Blues Ideas)"

All match. No silent contamination detected. **But the request-builder defect is real** and concurrent siblings on the same cohort are at highest risk. Suggest a follow-on ticket to audit the s4-statement request-builder (likely in `pipelines/master-distillation/queue/chapter_worker_step.py` or its helpers) and add an assertion that the request's `user_prompt` is composed from the current run_id's derived/ + llm-calls/ paths only.

- Pre-existing cmin9-drop2 / csus2 / csus4 baseline warnings unchanged from develop@088091d.

author: nmorabowen
body:
## Summary

Recovery PR for a hardening commit that was **stranded** when PR [#151](https://github.com/nmorabowen/OpenSees/pull/151) (true EAS) squash-merged just before the follow-up push landed. This re-homes it onto current `ladruno`.

`ladruno` HEAD currently has the EAS element with a **scale-dependent inner-Newton tolerance bug** that this PR fixes.

## The bug

`formEAStrue`'s inner Newton used an **absolute** tolerance `1e-10` on `‖∫MᵀσdV‖`. That residual has units force×length², so its converged magnitude scales with `E` and mesh size. At steel scale (E=2e5) it sits ~1e-7 — unreachable by 1e-10 — so **every EAS element logs "did not converge" every step** (300k+ warnings on a real model). The PR-2 unit tests only passed because they use E≈1e3.

## Fix
- **Relative criterion:** converge when `‖∫MᵀσdV‖ ≤ tolRel·r0 + tolAbs` (`tolRel=1e-8`, `r0` = first-iteration residual, `tolAbs` floor for the uniform-strain case); condense against the **converged** `Kaa`.
- **New regression test** `test_eas_drives_j2_lemaitre_damage`: EAS drives a path-dependent + softening material (`LadrunoJ2 -damage lemaitre`) through full displacement on a homogeneous steel element, accumulating damage that matches `bbar` (both 8 GPs) — exercises the inner-Newton + commit cycle under plasticity+damage at steel scale.
- **ADR 19** records the `eas` vs `ssp`/`bbar`/`SSPbrick` damage comparison: `ssp` ≡ upstream `SSPbrick` under damage (peak within 0.08%); `bbar` resolves the ligament localization (8 damage points) where `ssp`'s single centroid point under-resolves; **`eas` hourglasses on the notched bar** (a known small-strain EAS instability) → use `ssp`/`bbar` for notched softening. EAS hourglass stabilization noted as a follow-up.

## Verification
Locally: EAS suite `tests/test_ladrunoBrick_eas.py` **7/7** (the 6 ADR §4 gates + the new damage test); the fixed code is byte-identical to the verified PR-2 build.

author: tanakakao
body:
## Summary

- Add filtering for automatically injected `DataContext` fields before constructing acquisitions through `BayesianOptimizer`.
- Keep only context fields explicitly accepted by the acquisition class `__init__` signature.
- Preserve explicit `acqf_kwargs`; only automatic `context_fields` are filtered.

## Why

After #53, `BayesianOptimizer` automatically fills `DataContext.X_baseline`. This can break acquisitions that do not accept `X_baseline` but have `**kwargs` and forward unknown kwargs to a BoTorch base class.

Example error:

```text
TypeError: MCAcquisitionFunction.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'X_baseline'
```

This occurred with:

```python
acq_config = AcquisitionConfig(name="UCB")
opt_config = OptimizeConfig(q=3, num_restarts=2, raw_samples=32)
candidates, acq_value = bo.candidate(acq_config, opt_config)
```

## Behavior

- `UCB`, `BALD`, etc. no longer receive unrelated automatic fields such as `X_baseline`.
- Acquisitions that explicitly accept context fields, such as EHVI / NEHVI-style acquisitions, still receive the fields they declare.

## Testing

- Not run in this environment.

author: masoodzaf
body:
## Why
E2E smoke was at **41/48**. The remaining 7 failures (each retried once) were **4 distinct root causes**, diagnosed against a CI-faithful local DB (`schema.sql` + all phases) with the real backend booted.

| # | Failing test | Root cause | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `adminFlows` tax-records → 500 | `admin.js` queried `debt_tax_amount`, which **phase-u dropped**; successor is `debt_securities_tax_amount` | **Real prod bug** |
| 2 | `onboarding` backfill | super_admin seeded *after* phase-r's `existing→true` backfill → got the `false` default | CI seed gap |
| 3 | `ratesAdmin` dup 409 **+** rates-bundle idempotent | `tax_rates_config` lacked `UNIQUE (tax_year, rate_type, rate_category)` | schema.sql drift |
| 4 | `excelRoundtrip` invariant | asserted `totalTaxChargeable === netTax + superTax`; product formula is `+ finalMinTaxChargeable` | Stale test |

## What
- **#1 (prod fix):** repoint the admin tax-records query to `debt_securities_tax_amount`. This endpoint **500s in prod today** (same class as the audit's BE-01).
- **#2:** seed the e2e super_admin with `onboarding_completed=true` (models a pre-wizard existing user).
- **#3 (root-cause fix):** add a guarded, PG-15-safe **deploy-reconciliation block** to `schema.sql` for the three constraints the live cluster carries hand-applied but `schema.sql` never shipped — `tax_returns.fk_user` CASCADE, `tax_returns (user_id, tax_year_id)` unique, and the `tax_rates_config` unique. A **fresh prod deploy would otherwise break** admin-delete, form-saves, and rates admin. These survive the phase loop (no phase recreates those tables), so the equivalent **band-aids were removed** from `backend.yml` + `e2e.yml`.
- **#4:** align the invariant to `taxCalculationService`'s actual composition.

### #3 and #4 each fix two failures
- The missing rates unique made the dup POST return 200 (not 409) **and** leave an orphan row the cleanup couldn't delete, which polluted the rates-bundle idempotency test (apply upserts, never deletes extras). The unique fixes both.

## Verified locally (throwaway postgres + real backend, CI-faithful init)
- Constraints survive `schema.sql` + full phase loop; `debt_tax_amount` gone, successor present.
- tax-records → **200**; onboarding login → **true**; exact dup sequence → **200 then 409, 0 orphans**; rates-bundle apply → **total_changes 0** (both applies).
- Full phase loop applies cleanly on top of the new constraints (no migration violates them).

author: hilalbursalii
body:
## Root cause

Two independent root causes across the 20 originally failing nightly tests, plus a structural flakiness fix applied on top:

### 1. `/jobs/activation` response shape (18 API tests + 1 cascade)

The v2 `POST /jobs/activation` response now returns a `priority` field on each
job. `priority` was added to the `ActivatedJobResult` schema in the product
OpenAPI spec (`zeebe/gateway-protocol/.../jobs.yaml`, `addedInVersion: "8.10"`,
required), but the test suite's generated response-shape spec
(`json-body-assertions/_generated/responses.json`) predates that addition and
did not declare it. Every test that activates a job therefore failed with:

```
Response shape errors for route POST 200 /jobs/activation:
[EXTRA] /jobs/0/priority is not declared in spec
```

This also caused the **element-instance-update** failure: on the first attempt
the update returned `204`, but the later `/jobs/activation` shape error
triggered a Playwright retry. Since `beforeAll` does not re-run on retry, the
retry hit a stale element instance and returned `409`.

### 2. Operate MI beforeAll listener selection (1 E2E test)

`Operate shows beforeAll execution listener on MI task...` selected the
multi-instance service task only via the diagram. For a multi-instance element
the diagram click does not resolve to a single flow node instance, so the
Listeners panel stayed scoped to the root process instance and returned no
listeners. The beforeAll execution listener job is attached to the MI body
element instance, not the root.

### 3. `process-instance-create-batch-to-migrate` structural flakiness

The batch migration tests were using an ever-growing `postMigrationAssertionOptions`
timeout (180s → 240s → 360s → 480s) to wait for Elasticsearch to reflect the
migrated `elementId` in `/user-tasks/search`. The test `With Multiple Filters`
failed on 2026-06-04 because:

- It ran immediately after the `Success` test, which had already generated a
  wave of ES indexing events from its own migration.
- `prepareTestCases` re-deployed `test_migration_process_v2.bpmn` on every test
  call (3×), adding more indexing events to the backlog per call.
- By the time post-migration verification started, ES had a large backlog and
  could not reflect the updated `elementId` within the 360s budget.

The root problem was the test polling the wrong signal: `/user-tasks/search`
goes through the slow secondary-storage indexer, while `/element-instances/search`
reflects engine state faster.

## Fix

**Shape fix (root cause 1):**
Add `priority` (`{"name":"priority","type":"number"}`) to the `/jobs/activation`
200 schema in `responses.json`, matching the OpenAPI spec and the existing
`/jobs/search` entry.

**E2E fix (root cause 2):**
In the MI listener E2E, after clicking the diagram node, select the
multi-instance body row in the instance history so the listeners panel
queries the correct `elementInstanceKey`. Follows the existing convention
in `processInstanceListeners.spec.ts`.

**Migration test redesign (root cause 3):**
- **Two-phase post-migration verification**: first gate on
  `searchElementInstanceByElementIdAndState` (60s) to confirm the engine moved
  the token, then verify `/user-tasks/search` with `postMigrationAssertionOptions`
  (120s). Per the migration docs, user tasks are preserved through migration with
  only their `elementId` updated — not deleted and recreated — so verifying the
  user-task API is a valid assertion. Gating on element-instance first means the
  indexing pipeline is already partially warm, so 120s is sufficient (vs the
  previous 480s blind-wait).
- **`elementId` added to the user-task search filter** when provided, so the poll
  only returns results once the correct element is indexed. Avoids intermediate
  states where `totalItems=1` but `elementId` is still stale, which burned retry
  budget unnecessarily.
- **v2 deployed once in `beforeAll`**: `processDefinitionKey` is read directly
  from the deploy result and shared across all tests. Previously `prepareTestCases`
  re-deployed on every call (3×), creating a new deployment version each time
  and leaving extra live instances on the shared cluster.
- **`postMigrationAssertionOptions` capped at 120s** and kept in
  `batch-operation-requestHelpers.ts` so it remains a shared, named constant
  rather than an inline escape hatch.

## Tests fixed (20 originally failing)

**E2E (1):**
- `tests/operate/multiInstanceBeforeAllListener.spec.ts` — Operate shows beforeAll execution listener on MI task and variables produced by beforeAll

**API (19), all caused by the `/jobs/activation` priority field:**
- `tests/api/v2/element-instance/element-instance-search-incident-api.spec.ts`
- `tests/api/v2/element-instance/element-instance-update-api.spec.ts`
- `tests/api/v2/incident/incident-resolve-api.spec.ts`
- `tests/api/v2/job/el-header-basic-tests.spec.ts` (2 tests)
- `tests/api/v2/job/el-header-cross-task-tests.spec.ts`
- `tests/api/v2/job/el-header-element-types-tests.spec.ts` (2 tests)
- `tests/api/v2/job/el-header-merge-conflict-tests.spec.ts`
- `tests/api/v2/job/job-api-tests.spec.ts`
- `tests/api/v2/job/job-completion-api-tests.spec.ts` (2 tests)
- `tests/api/v2/job/job-error-api-tests.spec.ts` (2 tests)
- `tests/api/v2/job/job-failure-api-tests.spec.ts` (2 tests)
- `tests/api/v2/job/job-update-api-tests.spec.ts`
- `tests/api/v2/job/mi-el-before-all-tests.spec.ts`
- `tests/api/v2/job/mi-el-start-end-tests.spec.ts`

## References

- Failing nightly E2E run: https://github.com/camunda/camunda/actions/runs/26860435581
- Failing nightly API (ES) run: https://github.com/camunda/camunda/actions/runs/26859682627
- Migration batch timeout failure: https://github.com/camunda/camunda/actions/runs/26925957367/job/79435995899
- Triage run: https://github.com/camunda/camunda/actions/runs/26865804444

Implements the approved spec ([docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-03-notifications-automations-design.md](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-03-notifications-automations-design.md)) and plan. Event-driven client + admin notifications across **email** (first-party Hostinger SMTP) and **in-app** (client portal feed + admin center), covering welcome / status / payment.

## What's included
- **Migration** (`2026_06_03_notifications.sql`) — one `notifications` table (feed + admin center + event log) with RLS (client reads own; admin via `is_admin()`); `notified_status` columns on `website_projects` + `brand_kits`. **Applied to prod + existing rows backfilled** so the watcher only fires on future transitions.
- **Email** (`api/_lib/email.js`) — nodemailer/Hostinger, DB-first creds (`getSetting`), `From` = `SMTP_USER` (avoids the 553 alias trap).
- **Engine + registry** (`api/_lib/notifications.js`, `notification-registry.js`) — `emitNotification()` inserts a row per recipient + best-effort email; never throws; 8 events.
- **Emit points** — inline: `client.created` (lead-convert + self-signup), `website.intake_submitted`, `invoice.paid`, `subscription.created`. Cron-watched (edge-function-driven): `website.done/failed`, `brandkit.logos_ready/done`.
- **Crons** (`?action=cron-notify-status` every 5 min, `?action=cron-admin-digest` daily) on the `website.js` router, `CRON_SECRET`-gated; registered in `vercel.json`.
- **UI** — client portal notification bell + feed (`PortalLayout`); admin `/admin/notifications` center + nav.

## Env to set (email is best-effort until then; in-app works regardless)
`SMTP_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS` (or `admin_settings`), `CRON_SECRET`, optional `ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL`.

## Verification
`npm run build` clean; `node --check` on all modified `api/*`; migration + backfill verified via Mgmt API; `is_admin()` confirmed to authorize the admin read path.

> Note: the VPS `codex/adversarial` diff-reviewer is billing-blocked (see memory); an independent `codex:rescue` pass was run on this branch.

author: pawankumar-ops
body:
### Motivation
- The community/chat feature needed a robust data model, secure APIs, and UI wiring so club communities and groups work reliably and persist messages.
- Ensure only authorized members and admins can create groups and post announcements to prevent unauthorized actions.
- Provide server-backed group message storage so conversations survive reloads and can be loaded on demand.
- Make the group/community creation UX reusable and consistent across chat and community flows.

### Description
- Reworked the data model in `models/Community.js` to add persisted `messages` on groups, stronger schemas and useful indexes for `clubId` and `members`.
- Replaced/implemented server APIs using NextAuth + MongoDB: `app/api/communities/route.js` (sync club communities, list/create communities), `app/api/communities/[id]/groups/route.js` (create groups with membership/admin checks), and added `app/api/communities/[id]/groups/[groupId]/messages/route.js` (GET/POST group messages with permission checks and trimming).
- Updated UI to call the new APIs and handle state: `components/CommunityPanel.jsx` now loads group messages, posts messages via the backend, shows loading/error states, auto-scrolls, and prevents non-admins from posting to announcement groups.
- Made the modal reusable by extending `components/NewGroupModal.jsx` with a `mode` option for creating communities or groups and updated `app/dashboard/chat/page.jsx` to use it for community creation; added small CSS utilities in `app/dashboard/chat/chat.css` for banner errors and disabled menu states.

### Testing
- Ran linting with `npm run lint`, which completed but produced project-wide warnings (no blocking errors). 
- Ran `npm run lint -- --quiet` which completed successfully with no reported problems.
- Attempted `npm run build` which failed during Next.js font fetch (Google Fonts for `Geist`/`Geist Mono`) due to an external network issue during build; the failure is environmental and unrelated to the community API/logic changes.

author: arrodes-bot
body:
## Fixes

### 1. exports is not defined in chess.js
chess.js 1.4.0 is a CommonJS module with no UMD build. Loading it via script tag fails because exports does not exist in the browser.

**Fix:** Added a module/exports shim before the script, then exposed Chess globally. Also fixed new chessjs() to new Chess() for the live training board.

### 2. SSE /api/train/stream connection failure
The Vercel API route was calling response.json() on the SSE streaming endpoint, which breaks the event stream.

**Fix:** Detect /train/stream path and proxy as raw text/event-stream using Response.body.getReader() instead of parsing JSON.

author: kaspernj
body:
## Problem

Websocket channel subscriptions resolved the request tenant **outside** a connection scope. In `_handleChannelSubscribe` (and the legacy `_handleChannelSubscription` resolver path), `_resolveTenant()` was called before `_withConnections(...)`.

Apps whose `tenantResolver` runs database queries — e.g. looking up a record's project and the caller's access — therefore borrowed a connection that could be checked back in before/while those queries ran. This surfaced intermittently as either:

- `Connection N doesn't exist any more - has it been checked in again?`, or
- a falsely **unauthorized** subscription (the access query returns nothing).

Frontend-model subscriptions avoid this because their `canSubscribe()` runs inside `_withConnections`; only the custom-channel tenant-resolution path was affected, so it went unnoticed until an app shipped a custom `VelociousWebsocketChannel` whose tenant resolution hits the database.

## Fix

Wrap tenant resolution in `_withConnections` in both subscription paths so the resolver's queries run within a held connection.

## Notes / follow-up

This removes the connection-lifetime race for the **single-subscription** case. There is a separate, still-open concurrency symptom (under many simultaneous subscriptions a default-DB access query can resolve against the wrong context) that needs per-subscription connection/DB-context isolation — tracked separately, not addressed here.

## Summary

- **README Pareto 図 (fidelity-vs-runtime) を maqina 0.14.0 で取り直し**。0.14.0 の adaptive controller 変更 (真の PI 化 / reject クランプ / 成長凍結, umbrella #148) を反映し, issue #158 で修正された wide dynamic range の **BDF tol-sweep 参照解** (自己収束 `bdf_pairwise_inf=[0,0]`) を使用。
- **`benchmarks/bench_readme_figure.py`**: #142 (3715acd) で混入した参照解形状チェック回帰 (`(1<<n,)` → `(1<<n)`, 実データで常に `ValueError`) を修正 + `--save-states-dir` 追加 (各 cell の最終状態 ψ(T) を problem/reference パス + sweep メタ + version 同梱の self-describing 圧縮 npz で保存; 参照解差替時に保存 ψ から infidelity 再計算可)。BDF primary 参照では Adams 不一致 WARNING を INFO に降格。
- **`scripts/run_bench_readme_0_14_0.sh`** (新規): Phase 1 (maqina, scenario 順次) + Phase 2 (QuTiP, 2 scenario 並列 `--blas-threads 1`) の一括実行。中断耐性・状態保存付き。
- **結果**: `benchmarks/results/0.14.0/` (maqina CSV + states 18) / `benchmarks/results/qutip/` (新 BDF 参照で再生成した QuTiP CSV + states 8, version 非依存共有 dir) / `docs/figures/0.14.0_pareto_{non_stiff,stiff}.png` (凡例に **QuTiP (Adams)** 明記) / `benchmarks/results/0.14.0/SUMMARY.md`。
- **`README.md`**: Performance 図を 0.12.0 → 0.14.0 に差し替え + SUMMARY リンク更新。
- **`docs/quickstart.md`**: Chebyshev `atol` 例を 1e-8 → 1e-6 (過剰精度の是正), §5 断熱性チェックの **Z2 縮退バグ修正** (k=1→k=2 縮退基底空間射影 + 断熱的な T=3000)。
- **`.gitignore`**: `results/{<X.Y.Z>,qutip}/states/*.npz` を track。

### 主要結果
- **wide dynamic range で Chebyshev が Krylov を同 atol で 6〜11× 高速**, reference 精度到達で **9.6× 高速** (per-step の Lanczos V 行列キャッシュ溢れ+直交化 vs 3 項漸化の差)。
- regression なし: 固定 cfm4 は infidelity 6 桁完全一致, adaptive 系は n_steps ±数〜15% (PI 化の保守化) で accuracy は atol 内。
- 詳細・解釈ノート (wall 帰属 / 相殺残差 / Adams 虚軸安定性) は SUMMARY.md (README には非掲載)。

## Test plan

- [x] `plot_readme_figure.py --version 0.14.0` が committed CSV (0.14.0 + qutip + 流用 cfm4) から 4 系列図を再生成 (unknown 系列警告なし)
- [x] `bench_readme_figure.py` の maqina API smoke (N=6, krylov/chebyshev/cfm4 3 method) 通過 + 状態 npz ラウンドトリップ (保存 ψ → 参照解 infidelity 再計算が保存値と一致)
- [x] 編集 python に ruff lint / format / ty 通過
- [x] main とのファイル重複なし (コンフリクトフリーでマージ可能) を確認
- [ ] レビュー: SUMMARY.md の解釈・acceptance 判定

## Post-apply actions

- **stiff 固定 cfm4 の ψ は本 run では欠落** (run がスクリプト更新 7f99e55 より前に起動したため; CSV 行は再生成済)。次回 README bench run で自動保存される。図/解析への影響なし。
- 実行環境: Intel Xeon Platinum 8470N (104 cores, HT off), OpenBLAS 0.3.26, BLAS/RAYON=default, maqina 0.14.0。

Closes #159

author: skrymer
body:
Closes #35.

## What this ships

Gives the user a glanceable sense of goal progress on `/today`, backed by a new per-aggregate progress endpoint. This is the **planned** half only — observed pace lands in slice E.

### Backend — `GET /api/goal/progress`
- New `GoalProgress` domain value object derives the planned fields from the active Goal + the **live, smoothed Trend Weight**: `kgToGo`, `percentComplete`, `plannedFinishDate` (= kg-to-go ÷ the Goal's rate), `plannedRateKgPerWeek`. Per ADR 0001/0002 the maths lives in the domain; the controller only loads the trend and presents it.
- Returns **404** when no active Goal exists. Before any weigh-in, falls back to the Goal's captured start weight.
- Pace fields (`paceStatus`, `observedRateKgPerWeek`, `observedFinishDate`) are present in the response shape but **null** for now.

### Frontend — `GoalGlanceTile` on `/today`
- Full-width card below `DaySummary`; the **whole card** links to `/review`. Shows `percentComplete` as the hero and `kgToGo`. No pace badge while pace is null.
- "Set a goal" CTA → `/profile` when there's no active Goal; renders nothing when Budget/Goal are absent, per the existing gating idiom.
- Refreshes after a dashboard weigh-in (a new reading nudges the trend).

### Docs
- CONTEXT.md gains the **Goal Progress** term + relationship. No new ADR — the work follows ADR 0001 (rich domain model) and ADR 0002 (backend computes, frontend presents).

## Tests
- Domain unit tests: kg-to-go, percent complete, planned finish, target-reached boundary (100% / 0 to go).
- API test: computed fields, 404 with no Goal, **smoothed trend not raw measurement**.
- Component tests: hero %, kg-to-go, whole-card link to `/review`, CTA when no Goal.
- Real-stack smoke (`goal-glance-tile.smoke.spec.ts`): seeds Goal + weights, asserts the tile matches the API's figures, taps through to `/review`, restores state — **Desktop + Mobile Chrome**.

## Verification
Walked through in a real browser at desktop (1280×900) and mobile (412×915): tile renders below the day summary with 40% / 3.0 kg to go, whole-card tap-through to `/review` works at both viewports, and editing the weight live-updated the tile (40%→80%). State restored afterward.
