author: trilamsr
body:
## Why

Every spec PR appended a row to `docs/engineer/specs/README.md`. With 6+ concurrent spec PRs the bottom of that file became a DIRTY-merge magnet — 8+ PRs hit it on 2026-06-02 alone (#567, #569, #571, #576, #577, #578, #579, plus the four ahead of them that landed and forced each later one to rebase). Each rebase invalidated the next PR's merge SHA. The cost was real: roughly 3 hours of cascade-rebase tax for one wave.

**Root cause**: the index lived in a single file at a single anchor, so N concurrent spec PRs all wrote the same byte range. Branch-protection's `strict=false` (`memory/feedback_branch_protection_strict`) does not help here because the contents-conflict is real, not a stale-base check.

**Fix (no symptom suppression)**: move source-of-truth into each spec file's own frontmatter (`title`, `status`, `summary`). The README becomes a derived artifact regenerated by `make specs-index`. Two parallel spec PRs now touch two different files; no shared anchor; no cascade.

## What changed

- **`scripts/gen-specs-readme.sh`** (243 LoC): filesystem-driven generator. Reads optional YAML-ish frontmatter on each `docs/engineer/specs/*.md` (skipping `README.md` itself); falls back to first H1. Sorts into three sections by `status:` (Active / Shipped / Archived); default `active`. `--check` mode for CI; `--specs-dir` + `--out` for tests.
- **`scripts/gen-specs-readme_test.sh`** (9 cases): determinism on same input, includes-all-specs, skips-README-itself, frontmatter-status-grouping, frontmatter-title-overrides-H1, AUTO-GENERATED banner present, filename-with-spaces handled, alphabetical-within-section, `--check` exit-1 on stale.
- **`Makefile`**: new `specs-index`, `specs-index-check`, `specs-index-test` targets; wired into the `check` target so `make check` catches a stale README.
- **`scripts/doc-check.sh`**: appended a specs-index freshness gate so `bash scripts/doc-check.sh` (pre-push) fails closed if the index is stale.
- **Backfilled frontmatter** into the 10 originally hand-curated specs (W6, unified-substrate, W7 UI, W9 redteam, adapters, PR-watcher, W2-c2, crypto-shred, W7 L4-review, OBS Wave-B) — preserves their long-form summaries verbatim.
- **`docs/engineer/specs/README.md`**: regenerated. Adds `AUTO-GENERATED` banner; preserves dependency graph, "what goes here", "what does NOT go here", "Related RFCs" tail; adds empty Shipped / Archived sections so the layout is stable when the first row lands.

## Followups for in-flight spec PRs

Open spec PRs (#567, #569, #571, #576, #577, #578, #579 — the ones that bit this session) will need a rebase that **drops their README edits**; the auto-generator will pick up their new spec file on next regen. Each of those PRs is a 1-line `git rebase` + `git reset HEAD~ -- docs/engineer/specs/README.md` away. Cascade-fix sweep lands next.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash scripts/gen-specs-readme_test.sh` — 9/9 pass
- [x] `bash scripts/doc-check.sh` — clean (specs-index freshness gate added)
- [x] `bash scripts/doc-check_test.sh` — 10/10 pass (regression)
- [x] `make check` — clean (~3 min, includes property-test sweep)
- [x] `make pre-push-check` — clean
- [x] Idempotency: two consecutive `bash scripts/gen-specs-readme.sh` runs leave zero diff
- [x] Stale detection: appending bytes to README -> `bash scripts/doc-check.sh` exits 1; regen -> exits 0
- [x] Filename-with-spaces fixture survives script (`spec-with spaces.md`)
- [ ] CI green (waiting)

## A+ scorecard (chore-tier)

| Dimension | Grade | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Root-cause fix | A+ | Shared-anchor pattern dissolved, not papered over. |
| TDD discipline | A | 9 cases written before generator; tests failed first, then passed. |
| Determinism | A+ | Idempotency verified twice; `LC_ALL=C sort`; no time/git-log inputs. |
| Adversarial review | A | Shell-injection (Python argv, no interpolation), shallow-clone (no git-log), filename-with-spaces (tested), hand-curated context (backfilled). |
| Deletion | B+ | Net +617/-18 LoC; tradeoff is generator+tests for infinite future rebase savings. |
| UX | A | `make specs-index` is one command; CI tells you when stale; frontmatter is self-documenting. |
| Reversibility | A | Drop the script + `make` targets + frontmatter blocks; README stays as-is. |

## Risk-tier addressed in-PR

- **Shell injection on filenames**: filenames pass through Python `sys.argv`, never `eval`/`bash -c`.
- **Frontmatter parser fragility**: only `title:` / `status:` / `summary:` recognized; unknown keys ignored; missing block falls through to H1; missing H1 falls through to filename.
- **Ordering nondeterminism across filesystems**: `LC_ALL=C sort` on `(status, filename)` keys.
- **Loss of hand-curated context**: backfilled 10 spec frontmatters from the prior README verbatim; remaining 24 fall through to H1 (none had a long summary in the prior README).
- **Shallow-clone CI breakage**: no `git log` dependency; pure filesystem.

```release-notes
[CHORE] specs README auto-generated from filesystem; manual edits ignored — eliminates the cascade-rebase storm pattern observed 2026-06-02 when 8+ parallel spec PRs all touched the same anchor at the bottom of `docs/engineer/specs/README.md`. Source-of-truth moves into each spec's optional YAML frontmatter (`title`, `status`, `summary`); regenerate with `make specs-index`. CI gate via `scripts/doc-check.sh` fails closed on stale index.
```

## What

An **integrated version** of the decision/critic agent subsystem + this session's work, plus two new features.

### 1. Integrated decision/critic learning loop (commit 1)
- Earnings-calendar scrape → **decision agent** (memory-weighted score → BUY/WATCH/PASS/IGNORE) → **price snapshots** → **critic agent** that updates `memory/key_knowledge_memory.json`. Reports surface in the app's **Reports** tab.
- Combined with this session's setup-signals / earnings-preview / company-TL;DR / **single-select event type** work.

### 2. Company cards (commit 2)
- A **separate company entity** (`company_cards` table + `app/assets/company_cards.json`), one card per ticker, with a real business intro: curated `COMPANY_TLDR` → **SEC SIC industry** (cached/capped) → `{size}-cap` fallback. No more market-cap jargon.
- Events carry `company_ticker`; the app links each card to a `CompanyModal` via a tappable **"About ›"**.
- First run: 1039 cards (29 curated / 244 SEC industry / 766 size — the long tail fills in over runs via the cache).

### 3. Continuously-learning earnings-alpha (commit 2)
- Per earnings event: **`pop_score`** (post-earnings *increase* likelihood) + **`lookahead_days`** (research-grounded pre-earnings-drift entry timing) → merged into the EVENT CALL block.
- **Learning loop**: `evaluate_outcomes` reads `investment_price_snapshots` for realized pre→post returns (`earnings_outcomes`); `learn` self-tunes thresholds + per-tier look-ahead in `memory/earnings_alpha_params.json`. Wired into `run_daily_agents.py`.

## Verification
- `run_daily_agents.py --skip-scrape` runs clean end-to-end (decision + critic + 9 snapshots + alpha + learning + export).
- App verified: single-select filter, company `About ›` modal, and the look-ahead/pop line render.

author: snackman
body:
## Summary
Surfaces each GPP party's existing fake-detection risk score (the same scorer that backs /underboss's review queue) as a two-level caution badge on the by-city payments table, and gates the **Send payment** action behind an extra confirmation when the party scores ≥30.

- **Two-level badge:** amber pill for `medium` (≥30), red pill for `high` (≥60), nothing below 30. Tooltip lists the top fired flags.
- **Applies to all payments pages** — they all render through `PaymentsAdminPage → PayoutsByPartyTable`, so the 7 regional wrapper pages are untouched.
- **Warn + confirm:** badge + tooltip on the table, AND an amber ack card in `SendPaymentModal` ("I've reviewed this event's fake-detection flags") that gates the Send button when the party is flagged.

## Backend
- New shared helper `backend/src/lib/fakeDetectionScan.ts` — `scorePartiesByIds(partyIds?)` + `buildSybilWalletSetFromDb()` extract the sybil pre-pass + party `findMany` + per-party `scoreEvent` block out of `underboss.routes.ts`. Scopes the query to a party-id set when provided, else all gpp (today's behavior).
- `GET /api/underboss/fake-detection` refactored to call the shared helper. **Response shape is unchanged** (still returns `meta.sybilWalletCount`).
- New `POST /api/admin/payouts/fake-detection-scores` in `admin-payout.routes.ts`. Body `{ partyIds: string[] }` (capped at 500). Returns a compact map keyed by party id: `{ score, tier, topFlags }`, with `clean` (score <10) entries omitted to keep the payload small.

## Auth choice
The new endpoint is guarded by **`requireAdminOrRegionalUnderboss()`** — the same guard the by-party payments feed uses — **not** the underboss `__admin__`-only gate. The regional payment portals (`/payments/latam`, etc.) are driven by regional underbosses, who would otherwise 403 on the score fetch and never see badges.

## Frontend
- New `FakeDetectionBadge` component (+ index export).
- `api.ts`: `fetchFakeDetectionScores()` + `FakeDetectionScoreMap` type.
- `PaymentsAdminPage`: best-effort, non-blocking score fetch keyed on the loaded by-city rows, guarded by its own sequence ref so a slow response can't clobber a newer filter. Passes `fakeScores` to the table and attaches the looked-up score to the send-payment target.
- `PayoutsByPartyTable`: renders the badge in the city-header pill strip.
- `SendPaymentModal`: amber warning card + `Checkbox` ack gating `canSubmit` when flagged; ack resets on recipient/amount change.

## Summary

Pulls the v0.2.1 fix from sowel-recipe-presence-display.

The recipe used to default state="awake" on every restart/toggle and never re-dispatch a wake until a full absence cycle completed. If the panel was physically at brightness=0 from a previous sleep, the next motion=true arriving while state="waiting" would silently transition to "awake" without dispatching wake — panel stayed dark.

The new build dispatches one unconditional display_wake at instance start (idempotent for already-awake panels, recovery for asleep ones). Encountered live on the kitchen display this morning after a Sowel container restart at 04:43Z.

body:
### Summary

Adds a new **Linear** (linear.app) data source plugin, plus its config-ui registration and a Grafana dashboard.

The plugin follows DevLake's 3-stage ETL using framework helpers:
- **Collect** (GraphQL → `_raw_linear_*`) via `NewStatefulApiCollector` + `CreateAsyncGraphqlClient` with rate-limit pacing; incremental collection uses a server-side `updatedAt` filter.
- **Extract** (`_raw_linear_*` → `_tool_linear_*`).
- **Convert** (`_tool_linear_*` → domain tables).

Scope = Linear **Team** → `ticket.Board`. Auth = personal API key (`Authorization: <key>`). Status is mapped deterministically from `WorkflowState.type` (no user-supplied mapping): `triage,backlog,unstarted → TODO`, `started → IN_PROGRESS`, `completed,canceled → DONE`.

Domain mappings:
- Team → `boards`
- Issues → `issues` + `board_issues` + `issue_assignees` (with assignee/creator names)
- Comments → `issue_comments`
- Labels → `issue_labels`
- Cycles → `sprints` + `sprint_issues`
- Issue history → `issue_changelogs`, and lead/cycle time derived from in-progress→done transitions
- Users → `accounts`

Also includes:
- **config-ui**: Linear connection form (endpoint + personal API key), Teams data scope backed by remote-scopes, and the scope-id mapping.
- **Grafana**: `grafana/dashboards/Linear.json` (per-tool dashboard, like Jira/Asana).

### Does this close any open issues?
Closes #8901

### Tests
- e2e `DataFlowTester` tests for every extractor and convertor under `backend/plugins/linear/e2e`, plus unit tests for status mapping, the incremental filter, scope/remote-scope mapping, and board/lead-time/long-title edge cases.
- `make build` and `golangci-lint run` are clean; the full `plugins/linear/...` suite passes against MySQL.

### Other Information
- All commits are DCO signed-off and use conventional commit messages.
- Edge cases covered: every `WorkflowState.type` (incl. triage/unknown→OTHER), unassigned issue, issue with no cycle, multiple labels, lead/cycle-time from history, resolution-before-creation guard, and long issue titles/URLs.

author: quanla93
body:
## Summary

- Agent now reads `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.{max,current,stat}` directly when a real cgroup memory limit is set, computing `used = current - file_cache` (Proxmox-style accounting). Fixes Docker-in-LXC, Docker-in-VM, and k8s pods where gopsutil's `/proc/meminfo` leaks the kernel host's RAM.
- Falls back to gopsutil when no real limit applies — bare-host behaviour unchanged.
- Startup `Warn` log when agent is inside a cgroup but `memory.max=max`, naming the exact knob to set (`mem_limit` for Docker, `lxc.cgroup2.memory.max` for LXC).
- Generated `docker-compose.yml` template gains a commented-out `mem_limit:` hint.

## Background

Reported by an operator whose Lumen UI showed 9router (Docker container running inside Proxmox LXC) stuck at RAM 60% while Proxmox said 7.5%. Root cause: Docker's `/proc/meminfo` does NOT inherit the LXC's lxcfs bind mount, so the agent saw the PVE host's 11.6 GiB total instead of the LXC's 4 GiB.

The host-side fix (`systemctl restart lxcfs` + container restart) addresses bare LXC agents, but Docker-in-LXC requires the agent to read cgroup directly — which is what this PR does.

## Test plan

- [ ] On bare host: agent reports same RAM% as before (gopsutil fallback)
- [ ] In Docker with `mem_limit: 4g` on a host with > 4 GiB RAM: agent reports container RAM% (e.g. 7%), not host (e.g. 60%)
- [ ] In Docker without `mem_limit`: agent logs `Warn` once at startup, RAM% falls back to host (unchanged)
- [ ] In LXC with lxcfs healthy: unchanged — `/proc/meminfo` shows container view, no cgroup path taken
- [ ] In LXC where `memory.max` is set explicitly: cgroup path takes over with correct values
- [ ] Swap follows same logic for `memory.swap.{max,current}`

author: adhorn
body:
## Summary

Step 6 of the execution phase described verify-after: operator runs the step, then a second person confirms before the next step unlocks. That made step 6 inconsistent with step 101 (which already says "ask the operator to confirm before running"), and contradicts the cognitive forcing function the skill articulates elsewhere.

For the steps where hold points matter most — irreversible actions, cutovers, destructive operations — verifying after the fact is an autopsy, not a barrier. The value is in the moment *before*: two minds on the same screen, the command and expected outcome read aloud, agreement that the action should proceed, then the operator runs it.

## Change

One-line rewrite of `change-management/SKILL.md` line 105 to align with step 101 (verify-before) and the underlying CSE principle.

`template.md` is already neutral on timing — no change needed there. `reference/preflight-questions.md` is unaffected.

## Why now

The Changebook reference implementation went through the same redesign recently — verify-after was removed in favor of verify-before because it was procedurally weak as a forcing function. The skill should be consistent with the principle it embodies.

author: fgrfn
body:
## Bug: miner list order changes by itself

**Reported:** the order of miners sometimes rearranges on its own (noticed with NMMiners). Desired: miners should always be listed by **hostname**, so the order only changes when a hostname is changed.

**Cause:** the backend polls devices concurrently and appends each result as it responds (`fetch_lottominer_safe` / `fetch_axehub_safe` use `results.append()` inside `asyncio.gather`), so the array order reflects *response timing* and jitters between refreshes. The frontend rendered that order as-is.

**Fix:** sort centrally in the store setters `setDevices` / `setAxeDevices` by **hostname** (falling back to name, then IP), with IP as a stable numeric tiebreaker. One change fixes all three surfaces — **Dashboard**, **Lottominer**, **AxeOS** — and the order now only changes when a hostname actually changes. (`localeCompare` with `numeric: true` so e.g. `nm2` sorts before `nm10`.)

### Verification
- Frontend: `npm run build` ✓, `npm run lint` ✓, `npm test` ✓ — **60 passed** (3 new store tests: hostname sort, name/IP fallback + tiebreak, AxeOS sort).

### Note
This sorts at the display layer, which fully resolves the user-visible jitter. The backend append-order itself is left as-is (it only affects Discord embed ordering, which is cosmetic) — happy to make the backend deterministic too if you'd like.

### 🛡️ Sentinel Security Improvement

This PR implements several defense-in-depth security enhancements focused on forensic auditability and input hardening.

#### 💡 Vulnerability / Enhancement
1.  **Forensic Visibility Gap**: Previously, audit logs used `req.path`, which could be truncated in catch-all handlers or when using sub-routers, losing critical context about the request target. Additionally, API 404s and unexpected server errors were not explicitly audited.
2.  **Unicode Obfuscation Risk**: The sanitization filter was missing several "invisible" formatting characters (like the Mongolian Vowel Separator and the full \u2060 block) which can be used to bypass filters or obfuscate malicious payloads.

#### 🔧 Fix details
-   **Hardened Logging**: Switched all security-relevant logging in `server.js` and `auth.js` to use `req.originalUrl`.
-   **Expanded Auditing**: Added `[audit] API_NOT_FOUND` and `[audit] SERVER_ERROR` logs with sanitized request metadata (method, URL, user, IP).
-   **Standardized Format**: Unified the log format across the app to ensure consistent parsing and searchability.
-   **Unicode Sanitization**: Updated the `CONTROL_CHARS` regex in `auth.js` to include modern invisible formatting characters.

#### ✅ Verification
-   **Automated Tests**: Ran `npm test`. All 91 tests passed, including new test cases for:
    -   API 404 audit logging.
    -   Sanitization of the Mongolian Vowel Separator and the `\u2060-\u206F` block.
    -   Verified that `req.originalUrl` is correctly captured in unit tests.

body:
Polish prompted by the earlier `401 Invalid API Key` run, where a bad key quietly failed all 40 tasks and printed a misleading `success=0`-looking output. An auth error is a global config failure, not a per-task one.

## Fix
- `agent.ErrUnauthorized` sentinel; the client returns it (wrapped) on HTTP 401/403 — **no retry** (a bad key won't fix itself).
- The eval aborts immediately with `errors.Is(err, agent.ErrUnauthorized)` → "fix the key and re-run (cached tasks resume; nothing was wasted)", instead of logging a doomed run per task.

## Tests
Offline: `TestOpenAIChatUnauthorizedIsTyped` (401 → `errors.Is ErrUnauthorized`, exactly one call, no retry). Full suite green; `gofmt` clean; eval compiles.

## Note
Pure robustness — does not affect a run with a valid key. **Not required** for the in-progress free-tier run; mergeable whenever.

body:
Spec for Subsystem E of the broader parity initiative — final subsystem.

## Scope (narrowed)

OTel semantic conventions moved to Subsystem C; protocol conformance moved to Subsystem B. What remains in E:

1. **License audit & policy** — tiered allow / warn / deny SPDX classification across both modules.
2. **CycloneDX SBOM** — per-binary + per-image; release-attached; nightly cron.
3. **SLSA Build Level 2 provenance** — via `slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator`.
4. **Sigstore release signing** — keyless cosign for binaries and container images.
5. **Apache Arrow IPC roundtrip** + **CNCF Observability category alignment doc**.

## License policy

- `tests/community-standards/license-policy.yaml` — SPDX tiers (allow: MIT/Apache/BSD/ISC; warn: LGPL/MPL/EPL/CDDL; deny: GPL/AGPL/SSPL/BUSL).
- `docs/LICENSE_EXCEPTIONS.md` — single source of truth for accepted warn-tier deps with rationale + linking-model + verified date.
- CI workflow blocks PRs introducing deny-tier or unexcepted warn-tier licenses.

## Supply chain

- `cyclonedx-gomod` produces per-binary SBOM; `syft` produces per-image SBOM.
- `slsa-github-generator` produces signed provenance attestations.
- `cosign` keyless OIDC signs binaries (`.sig` + `.crt`) and images (signature in OCI registry).
- `docs/SUPPLY_CHAIN.md` ships operator-facing verification commands (`cosign verify`, `slsa-verifier verify-artifact`).

## Migration

5 PRs (E1–E5):
- E1: license policy + audit + first CI gate.
- E2: CycloneDX SBOM workflow.
- E3: Arrow IPC roundtrip test.
- E4: SLSA L2 provenance + Sigstore signing.
- E5: CNCF alignment doc + governance polish + verify-release Makefile target.

## Relationship to other subsystems

- Depends on Subsystem C (Arrow roundtrip uses LH parquet writer).
- Closes out scope items deferred from earlier subsystems.

## Scope

Design only — no code changes. Implementation plan added in same PR.

author: proggeramlug
body:
## What

Reading a collection method off an *instance* (`const m = s.forEach`) now returns
the same brand-checking thunk installed on `Set.prototype`, so:
- `m.call(badReceiver)` throws a `TypeError` (was: silently did nothing), and
- `s.forEach === Set.prototype.forEach` holds.

## Why

The instance read resolved via `js_class_method_bind`, producing a closure
**pre-bound to the instance**. A later `m.call(0)` kept the bound Set, so the
brand check saw a valid receiver and never threw. test262's collection suites
assert exactly this (`Set/prototype/forEach/this-not-object-throw-*`,
`does-not-have-setdata-internal-slot-*`, etc.), each with a
`s.method.call(badThis)` second assertion.

## How

New `collection_proto_method_value(builtin, method)` in `collection_proto_thunks.rs`
fetches the already-installed thunk value off the `<Builtin>.prototype` singleton
(mirrors the existing `primitive_proto_method_value`). The Set instance
method-value read in `field_get_set.rs` returns that instead of the bound closure,
falling back to the legacy path if unavailable.

## Verification

- **test262 `built-ins/Set`: 103 → 26** runtime-fails of 180.
- Byte-identical to `node --experimental-strip-types`: `s.forEach.call(0)` throws
  TypeError; `s.forEach === Set.prototype.forEach`; the original failing assembled
  test exits clean.
- **No regression**: direct `s.forEach(cb)` / `s.add` / `m.forEach` (codegen
  fast path to `js_set_foreach`, separate from the value read) unaffected.
- `perry-runtime` suite 974/974 (two pre-existing flaky tests — url-cwd and a
  typed-array search — pass in isolation; this PR touches neither file).
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; file-size gate clean; rebased on main.

## Scope note

Map/WeakMap/WeakSet instance brand checks already throw correctly (they route
differently); this PR targets the Set instance-read path.

### go-git: Improper single-quote escaping in go-git SSH transport
[CVE-2026-45570](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-45570) / [GHSA-m7cr-m3pv-hgrp](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-m7cr-m3pv-hgrp)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

`go-git`'s SSH transport constructs the remote exec command by wrapping the repository path in single quotes without escaping single quotes embedded inside the path. This diverges from canonical Git, which shell-quotes the path through `sq_quote_buf` so that an embedded `'` becomes the `'\''` close-escape-reopen sequence and the whole path round-trips as a single quoted argument.

A repository path containing a single quote can therefore break out of the quoted region in the exec command and be appended as additional shell tokens. On SSH servers that evaluate the exec command through a shell (for example a user account whose login shell is `/bin/sh` or `/bin/bash`, or a `ForceCommand` wrapper that re-evaluates `$SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND`), those additional tokens execute in that account's command-execution context. SSH servers that tokenize the exec command without shell evaluation, including the canonical `git-shell` setup, are not affected.

The vulnerable behaviour is on the SSH server side, not in `go-git`: the same bytes can be produced by any SSH client. The change in `go-git` is defense-in-depth that restores parity with canonical Git's wire format and prevents `go-git` from being a vehicle for reaching shell-evaluating servers through attacker-influenced repository paths.

##### Patches

Users should upgrade to a patched version in order to mitigate this issue. The fix ports `sq_quote_buf` from canonical Git into `go-git`'s SSH transport so that the wire output is byte-identical to what `git` itself would send for the same input.

Versions prior to `v5` are likely to be affected, users are recommended to upgrade to a supported go-git version.

##### Credit

Thanks to @​N0zoM1z0 for reporting this to the `go-git` project. :bow:

- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:P/VC:N/VI:N/VA:N/SC:L/SI:L/SA:L`

### go-git: Crafted repositories may modify main and submodule .git directories
[CVE-2026-45571](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-45571) / [GHSA-crhj-59gh-8x96](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-crhj-59gh-8x96)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact
A path validation issue in `go-git` could allow crafted repository data to affect files outside the intended checkout target, including the repository's `.git` directory.

These validations were introduced in upstream Git years ago, so the vulnerability arose from go-git drifting from those checks. Some attack vectors were platform-specific: certain payloads affected only Windows users, others affected only macOS users, and some applied across all supported platforms.

Using non-descendant `go-billy` filesystem instances, or different filesystem types, for the `Storer` and `Worktree` may provide some isolation against `.git` directory manipulation. For example, users that store the `.git` directory through `memfs` while using `osfs` for the worktree are not affected by this vulnerability in the main repository, because repository metadata is not materialized inside the worktree filesystem.

However, this isolation does not necessarily apply when the repository contains submodules, since submodule dotgit directories may still be represented or materialized within the worktree context.

It is important to note that exploitation requires a maliciously crafted repository payload. Users should always exercise caution when interacting with repositories or Git servers they do not trust.

##### Patches
Users should upgrade to a patched version in order to mitigate this vulnerability. Versions prior to `v5` are likely to be affected, users are recommended to upgrade to a supported go-git version.

##### Credits
Thanks to @​kodareef5, @​AyushParkara and @​N0zoM1z0 for reporting this to the go-git project in three separate reports. 🙇

### go-git: Malformed Git object data may cause panics or resource exhaustion
[GHSA-w5pp-99ch-qj29](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-w5pp-99ch-qj29)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact
Several denial-of-service issues were identified in `go-git` when parsing maliciously crafted Git repository data.

An attacker may craft a malicious `.pack`, `.idx` or loose objects that causes an application using an affected version of `go-git` to panic or consume excessive resources.

This can lead to denial of service in applications that use `go-git` to clone, fetch, open, or otherwise process untrusted repositories or Git object data.

Exploitation requires the ability to alter read-only files such as `.pack` or `.idx` from the local repository's `.git/objects/pack/` directory. Alternatively, the user would need to be interacting with a malicious remote server, which is not recommended and exposes users to a broader class of security risks beyond this issue.

body:
## Summary

PR-B of the two-PR #134 split, stacked on PR-A (#136). It makes `cuasmR`
CRAN-ready (Phase 6): roxygen-generated docs, declared dependencies, and a
clean `R CMD check --as-cran`. Pure packaging/polish — the only runtime
change is an error-path fix in `run_bench()` (below).

**Base = the PR-A branch** (`feat/134-cuasmr-measurement-migration`), so the
diff shows only Phase 6. GitHub retargets this to `main` when #136 merges.

## Changes

### Packaging
- `roxygen2::roxygenise()`: generated `man/` (20 `.Rd`) and took ownership of
  `NAMESPACE` — **export set unchanged** (same 20 functions, verified by set
  diff). `RoxygenNote` 7.3.3.
- `DESCRIPTION`: declared `Imports: jsonlite, stats, utils` (previously
  undeclared); Title `cubins` -> `Cubins`.
- Added `NEWS.md` (0.2.0 measurement API + 0.1.0), `cran-comments.md`
  (documents the 3 benign NOTES), and `.Rbuildignore`.

### Source correctness (surfaced by `R CMD check`)
- `run_bench()`: the error path ran the invalid
  `attr(character(0), "status") <- 1L`. This does **not** silently read `rc = 0`
  (a post-merge review corrected the original wording here): `attr(<literal>, k)
  <- v` is not a valid assignment target — it *throws* `target of assignment
  expands to non-language object`. Because that throw happens **inside** the
  `tryCatch` error handler, it is uncaught and propagates out of `run_bench()`,
  aborting the whole measurement harness with a misleading message. Now
  `structure(character(0), status = 1L)` -> `rc = 1` on the can't-launch path,
  which `validate_sample()` records as `crash(exit=1)`. The handler only fires
  when the command cannot be launched at all (a non-zero exit or a fired timeout
  return *normally* with a status attr, so the handler is never invoked), so this
  converts a misleading propagating crash into the intended graceful per-sample
  invalidation — strictly more correct.
- `bench_meta.R`: qualified `utils::modifyList` (bareword -> "no visible global
  function definition" NOTE); replaced the degree sign with a `°` escape
  in two `sprintf()` strings (non-ASCII in code -> portability WARNING).
- Replaced em-dash with `--` in roxygen/comment text across the bench files.

## `R CMD check --as-cran`

```
0 errors | 0 warnings | 3 notes
```

All three NOTES are benign (documented in `cran-comments.md`):
- New submission.
- Title-case flags `sm_8x` -> `Sm_8x`: a false positive; `sm_8x` is the NVIDIA
  architecture token (`nvcc -arch=sm_86`), not a word.
- timestamps / pandoc: properties of the check environment, not the package.

## Verification
- testthat: **126 expectations, 0 failures** (run twice, stable) — GPU-free
  differential/unit tests plus the nvdisasm roundtrip.
- Pre-push gate green on push (7 configs, 0 regressions).

## Scope
`bench_flash_all.R`'s `run_bench` (the deferred dup from PR-A's AC4) is still
**not** migrated — out of scope for CRAN polish, a separate follow-up.

Refs #134 — leaves the epic open; it can be closed once both PRs land and the
`bench_flash_all` follow-up is decided.

The exact repro in the issue (add sender **from the incoming message** under a different nickname → reply doesn't resolve) stayed broken.

## Root cause

`add_sender_to_address_book` (app.rs) → `ImportContact::opened_with` handed over only the bs58 inbox address. A bare address carries no card metadata, so the modal opened with a **blank nickname**; the user picked an arbitrary local label and nothing tied the reply back to the sender.

## Fix

- `ImportContact` gains `prefill_alias: Option<String>`; `opened_with(address, alias)`.
- `add_sender_to_address_book` threads `Message.from` (sender display name) through, trimming blank names to `None`.
- The import modal's prefill effect **defaults the local nickname** to that display name.

**Mechanism (corrected after review):** the *primary* fix is the `local_alias` default — a reply is prefilled `to: Message.from`, so it now matches the contact's `local_alias` **exactly**. `suggested_alias` is the *relabel fallback*: the effect also seeds `card_suggested_alias`, but the save path (`persisted_suggested_alias`) intentionally **drops** it when it equals the local nickname (accept-default case — storing a duplicate is pointless). It's persisted only when the user **relabels**, so a reply to the original display name still resolves via #295.

## Reproducing tests

- `opened_with_carries_sender_alias_for_289` — pins the constructor seam.
- `persisted_suggested_alias_kept_only_on_relabel_289` — pins the save-path dedup rule (relabel persists, accept-default drops, None/empty → None). Confirmed **red** when the dedup is removed.
- `lookup_resolves_by_sender_alias_when_suggested_preserved_289` (#295) — the resolver fallback the relabel case feeds.

## Review

Reviewed by skeptical + code-first subagents. They caught that the original comments/test overclaimed the suggested_alias mechanism; this is corrected — the docs now state local_alias-primary and the save-path dedup is unit-tested. No runtime defects found (no double-move across the two onclick closures; real-card metadata not clobbered; prefill cleared so no leak into later manual paste).

## Not covered

A full Playwright add-from-message→reply E2E needs a verified-unknown sender fixture (heavy/flaky in the offline synth-pubkey suite). Deferred to #291's coverage debt.

## Test
`cargo test -p freenet-email-ui --lib` → 189 passed. Clippy clean on default + `example-data,no-sync`.

### Inefficient candidate hostname parsing in crypto/x509
[CVE-2026-27145](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-27145) / [GO-2026-5037](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5037)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
(*x509.Certificate).VerifyHostname previously called matchHostnames in a loop over all DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. This caused strings.Split(host, ".") to execute repeatedly on the same input hostname.

With a large DNS SAN list, verification costs scaled quadratically based on the number of SAN entries multiplied by the hostname's label count. Because x509.Verify validates hostnames before building the certificate chain, this overhead occurred even for untrusted certificates.

#### Severity
Unknown

author: maduranga98
body:
QR codes are scanned at physical machines, so they must never point at localhost. The base URL was taken from VITE_APP_URL at build time, which defaults to http://localhost:5173 in .env.example — so local builds baked localhost into the QR.

Resolve the base URL at runtime instead: prefer the actual serving origin when it is not localhost (self-correcting for deployed builds), then a non-localhost VITE_APP_URL, then the hardcoded production URL. QR codes are regenerated live on the QR page, so this fixes every machine immediately.

author: dkgoutham
body:
Builds on #30. Adds transceiver-focused localnet integration coverage, folds it into the existing test areas, and hardens the shared harness. Every test is `#[ignore]`-gated and runs against a real stack (Wormhole core + transceiver + manager + token).

### Transceiver coverage
- **Harness:** transceiver-targeted `Stack` methods (remove/disable transceiver, pause/unpause, two-step ownership, peer set/enable) and a tampered-signature VAA builder.
- **Inbound rejection barriers:** tampered signature (20), unexpected emitter (35), unexpected recipient manager (33), disabled peer (14) — consolidated into one `receive_rejects.rs` sharing setup + struct-update perturbation.
- **Admin scenarios:** transceiver pause blocks inbound/outbound, two-step ownership re-gates `set_peer`, and disabling a transceiver auto-adjusts the manager threshold.

### Cleanup / refactor
- Drop unused broadcast/quote `Stack` methods.
- Bundle `send_transfer`'s message params into a struct, removing the `clippy::too_many_arguments` allow.
- Friendbot funding blocks on account visibility to remove a startup race.
- Centralize the shared "standard peer" constants and the inbound-VAA builder into `tests/common`, replacing per-file copies.
- Unify event-poll timeouts into a single `EVENT_TIMEOUT`.

### Review fixes
- Queued-transfer completion polls the on-chain release gate (ledger time) instead of a fixed wall-clock sleep that could flake on slow CI.
- `build-wasms.sh` removes stale artifacts before `--optimize`, so the oversized unoptimized manager wasm is never uploaded (the network rejected it as `TxSorobanInvalid`).
- Tighten three assertions: locking outbound uses a two-sided balance bound (catches over-debit while tolerating gas); queued completion matches `transfer_sent` on the queued amount (the primer transfer also emits one); replay asserts `message_already_executed`.

### Verification
```bash
# static + unit + wasm build
cd stellar
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
stellar contract build

# localnet integration suite (all #[ignore] tests)
cd integration-tests
./scripts/start-localnet.sh && ./scripts/fund-identity.sh
./scripts/run-tests.sh        # 30 passed
./scripts/stop-localnet.sh
```

author: oopslink
body:
## #185 FINDING-L: agent reply turn errored (post_message authz dual-id mismatch)

Base: `v2.7-integration`. Release-blocker. The wake chain now reaches the agent (emit→projector→agent.converse→worker→claude inject), but the agent's **reply turn errored** — its `post_message` call returned **403 not_a_participant**.

### Root cause
`agentActor(a)` returned the **execution-entity** ref (`agent:<entity-id>`), but conversation participants — and project membership — carry the agent's **identity-member** ref (`agent:<member-id>`, the business id, per #77). So `agentIsActiveParticipant` compared an entity ref against a member-ref participant → never matched → the reply was rejected and the turn failed.

### Fix
`agentActor` now returns the **member ref** (`a.IdentityMemberID()`) when set, falling back to the entity id only for an agent with no member (shouldn't occur post no-middle-state). It is the single business identity used as the **message sender**, the **observability Actor**, and the **pm IdentityRef**, so it also:
- stops the entity ULID leaking as the agent's message **sender** (member-id everywhere / Tester zero-leak gate), and
- makes `block_task`/`complete_task`'s pm actor **match** the agent's project membership (granted under the member ref by the assign flow).

The task-wake self-exclusion already matches both ref forms (#77), so the member-ref sender is still correctly excluded (no self-wake / ping-pong).

### Test
`TestAgentActor_PostMessageAuthz_UseMemberID` — `agentActor` yields the member ref; an agent with a member-ref participant passes authz; a non-participant is rejected. Closes the **missing post_message test** gap that let FINDING-L through (the #185 path had no participant-authz test). `go build/vet/test ./...` green, gofmt clean.

author: vercel[bot]
body:
## Vercel Web Analytics Installation - Implementation Report

### Summary
Successfully installed and configured Vercel Web Analytics for the Kleid project, a vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript fashion store website.

### Framework Detection
The project is a **vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript application** with no framework or build system:
- No package.json or node_modules
- Simple static site with index.html, style.css, and script.js
- Uses CDN-hosted libraries (Bootstrap, GSAP)

### Implementation Details

#### Approach Used
Based on the latest Vercel documentation (fetched June 3, 2026), I implemented the **vanilla JavaScript approach** for projects without a package manager or framework:

1. **Web Analytics**: Added script initialization and loader to track page views and visitor analytics
2. **Speed Insights**: Added performance monitoring to track Core Web Vitals and page performance metrics

#### Files Modified
- **index.html**: Added Vercel Analytics scripts to the `<head>` section

#### Changes Made
Added the following script tags in the head section (after Bootstrap CDN, before the title tag):

```html
<!-- Vercel Web Analytics -->
<script>
    window.va = window.va || function () { (window.vaq = window.vaq || []).push(arguments); };
</script>
<script defer src="/_vercel/insights/script.js"></script>

<!-- Vercel Speed Insights -->
<script>
    window.si = window.si || function () { (window.siq = window.siq || []).push(arguments); };
</script>
<script defer src="/_vercel/speed-insights/script.js"></script>
```

### Key Implementation Notes

1. **No Package Manager Required**: For vanilla HTML projects, Vercel Analytics doesn't require npm/pnpm installation. The scripts are served directly from Vercel's infrastructure when the site is deployed.

2. **Script Placement**: Scripts are placed in the `<head>` section with `defer` attribute to ensure non-blocking loading.

3. **Queue Pattern**: The initialization scripts use a queue pattern (`window.vaq` and `window.siq`) to buffer analytics calls until the main scripts load.

4. **No Build Step**: Since this is a static HTML site, no build process or dependency installation was needed.

### Testing Considerations

The analytics will become active once the site is deployed to Vercel:
- Web Analytics will track page views, visitor counts, bounce rates, and referrer data
- Speed Insights will monitor Core Web Vitals (LCP, FID, CLS) and other performance metrics
- To test locally, you can use an incognito browser window after deployment
- Analytics data may take a few hours to appear in the Vercel dashboard

### Activation Steps Required

To activate analytics on Vercel:
1. Deploy the site to Vercel using `vercel deploy`
2. Enable Web Analytics in the Vercel dashboard under the Analytics tab
3. Monitor the Network tab in browser DevTools for requests to `/_vercel/insights/` to verify functionality

### Documentation Sources
- Official Vercel Analytics Quickstart: https://vercel.com/docs/analytics/quickstart
- Vercel Community Discussion: https://community.vercel.com/t/using-vercels-analytics-with-no-framework/3194
- Documentation fetched on: June 3, 2026

author: koku-ci-triager-bot
body:
## GlitchTip
https://glitchtip.devshift.net/insights-hccm-stage/issues/4111528

## Classification
code_fixable

## Summary

`Provider.set_data_updated_timestamp()` called `self.save(update_fields=["data_updated_timestamp"])`, which Django translates to `UPDATE ... WHERE pk = <uuid>`. When 0 rows are affected (because the provider was deleted between the caller's `.filter().first()` check and this save), Django raises `DatabaseError: Save with update_fields did not affect any rows.`

This is a classic TOCTOU race: `update_cost_model_costs` does `if provider := Provider.objects.filter(...).first(): provider.set_data_updated_timestamp()` — but the provider can be deleted in the window between those two lines.

**Fix:** Replace `self.save(update_fields=["data_updated_timestamp"])` with a queryset `.update()` call, which returns 0 silently when no row is found rather than raising.

author: vivek7405
body:
Closes #256

## What

An app deployed under a sub-path (example.com/app/) behind a proxy that does not strip the prefix was broken: every framework-emitted absolute URL (importmap targets, modulepreload hints, the boot script's `/__webjs/core/*` specifiers and per-route module URLs, the server-action RPC fetch, the dev reload stream) assumed the app sat at the origin root, so they 404d and the page never hydrated. `createRequestHandler` explicitly targets embedding, where a sub-path mount is the norm.

Add `webjs.basePath` with a **strip-at-ingress + prefix-on-emit** model, two seams only:

- **Strip at ingress**: at the very start of request handling the base path is stripped from the request URL, so all downstream routing, the `/__webjs/*` checks, the source-file gate, redirects, and trailing-slash see a root-relative path and work unchanged. A path not under the base path 404s.
- **Prefix on emit**: every framework-emitted same-origin absolute URL is prefixed through one `withBasePath` helper, leaving cross-origin CDN targets alone.

Empty basePath (the default) makes both seams pure no-ops, so an unconfigured app is byte-identical, guarded differentially and verified live against the dogfood apps. A hostile value (traversal, a protocol, a network-path `//host`) fails safe to no base path. The key is typed into the `webjs.*` config schema and `WebjsConfig`.

## Completeness (the part the review hardened)

The headline failure is "one framework-emitted URL left bare 404s under the sub-path". The self-review swept for exactly that, in three rounds:

- **Round 1** caught the **server-action RPC stub** fetching a bare `/__webjs/action/...` (every server action would break). Fixed and covered.
- **Round 2** caught the **dev live-reload `EventSource('/__webjs/events')`** (live-reload would break under a sub-path proxy). Fixed and covered.
- **Round 3** produced an exhaustive table of every framework-emitted client URL (importmap, vendor, integrity, boot specifiers, lazy-loader, modulepreload, reload src + stream, RPC, early hints) confirming each is prefixed, and every bare one is genuinely author-supplied, server-side, or client-router navigation. Clean.

## Out of scope (documented follow-up)

Author-written `<a href="/about">` links and client-router navigation prefixing are not auto-prefixed, the same boundary Next draws between auto-prefixing `Link` vs a raw `<a>`. Noted in the docs.

## Tests

`packages/server/test/base-path/` (18): the normalizer; the key integration test that GETs every emitted same-origin URL under `/app` and asserts each resolves <400 (the exact thing that 404s on a broken sub-path deploy); route resolves with the prefix and 404s without; core runtime under the prefix; the RPC stub fetch is prefixed (bare path 404s, prefixed reaches the endpoint); the dev reload EventSource is prefixed; and the byte-identical empty-default no-op. Config drift + type fixture include `basePath`. Full suite 1915. Blog e2e 69/69 (the empty-default no-op in a real browser). e2e for the prefixed case is N/A because the HTTP-layer test GETs every module URL a browser would fetch under the prefix and asserts it resolves, which is the exact failure mode.

## Dogfood

website / docs / ui-website boot with bare `/__webjs/*` URLs (no stray prefix) and all preloads resolve; blog e2e 69/69. No version bump (batched core/server release).

updated live-match generation in `handlers/match.py` to pass `s.get('stadium')` into card generators. - Updated admin preview endpoint (`admin_scorecard_preview` in `admin.py`) to accept a transient `color` query param (validated via regex) so the page can display an unsaved color preview. - Updated the admin settings template (`templates/admin_scorecard_settings.html`) to show "Website preview", add `data-base-src` to preview ``, and include JS (`refreshScorecardPreview`) to update the preview on color `input`/`change` and when choosing preset swatches. ### Testing - Ran the project's automated test suite with `pytest -q`, which completed successfully. - Executed the scorecard-render smoke test (`tests/test_scorecard_render.py::test_batting_and_bowling_render`) against the new renderer and it passed, confirming PNG generation for batting and bowling cards. - Verified the admin preview endpoint accepts `color=#rrggbb` queries and returns a 200 PNG response in automated integration checks. ------ [Codex Task](https://chatgpt.com/codex/cloud/tasks/task_e_6a1fea7d9afc8329818bec15ccc29f8d)

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements the first five items from `IMPROVEMENTS.md` in the training/inference stack, then reorders the roadmap so prior items 6–10 become 1–5 and adds five new candidate improvements.

- **Training policy upgrade (items 3–4)**
  - Switched from `PPO` to `RecurrentPPO` (`MlpLstmPolicy`) for temporal memory across tricks.
  - Added `TransformerCardExtractor` (`models.py`) to encode hand/trick card structure before policy/value heads.
  - Wired extractor through `policy_kwargs` in `train.py`.

- **Self-play robustness (item 1)**
  - Replaced fixed opponent randomness with an epsilon curriculum (`OPPONENT_EPSILON_START -> OPPONENT_EPSILON_END`).
  - Kept league-style opponent sampling and hardened checkpoint compatibility fallback for mixed checkpoint formats.

- **Observation model expansion (item 2)**
  - Expanded env observation from 171 to 340 dims in `whist_env.py`.
  - Added per-seat played-card planes, lead-suit signal, trump-void flags, and trick-position one-hot.
  - Updated env info payload to expose inferred trump-void state.

- **Inference-time search (item 5)**
  - Added lightweight root MCTS in `play.py` using policy priors + value estimate + rollout scoring.
  - Exposed runtime control via `--mcts-sims` (default enabled).

- **Roadmap/documentation alignment**
  - Updated `IMPROVEMENTS.md`: promoted old 6–10 to new 1–5 and appended five new future improvements.
  - Updated `README.md` for new observation schema, recurrent/transformer training architecture, and MCTS usage.
  - Added `sb3-contrib` to `requirements.txt`.

Example (new inference entrypoint with search control):

```bash
python play.py --mode watch --mcts-sims 64
```

author: ebibibi
body:
## Summary

X mobile apps no longer handle `x.com/intent/tweet` deep links, so the one-click
"post to X" link only works in desktop browsers — on mobile the link opens X but
does not pre-fill the composer (other apps behave the same way).

This makes the post text **copyable directly from Discord** so mobile users can
copy and paste into the X app:

- The full post text now goes in the Discord **message body** as a fenced code
  block. Discord renders a copy control for body code blocks (desktop hover /
  mobile long-press). Previously the text lived inside an embed, where no copy
  control is shown — that was the root cause.
- The 200-char preview truncation is removed; the full text is sent.
- A **dynamic backtick fence** is used so a post containing ``` does not break
  the code block, keeping the copied text byte-for-byte identical to the original.
- Very long posts (beyond Discord's 2000-char message limit) are split into
  **numbered messages** instead of being silently truncated.
- The desktop one-click intent link is kept as an embed for browsers where it
  still works.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_x_intent_service.py` — 17 new tests pass
- [x] Live test post sent to the x-intent Discord channel with the new format
- [ ] Mobile: long-press the code block → Copy → paste into the X app
- [ ] Desktop: hover the code block → copy button works; embed link still opens
      a pre-filled X composer

author: adrianmiguel99
body:
Implementación de validación de disponibilidad de vuelos y control de ocupación de asientos. Esta funcionalidad permite verificar si existen campos disponibles antes de continuar con la compra y antes de procesar el pago, además de registrar la ocupación de asientos por clase en cada vuelo.

# Cambios Realizados

## Base de Datos
- Se agregaron las columnas `occupiedFirstclass` y `occupiedTurist` a la tabla `Flight`.
- Creación del Stored Procedure `CheckFlightAvailability` para validar disponibilidad de campos según la capacidad de la aeronave.
- Creación del Stored Procedure `ReserveFlightSeats` para actualizar la cantidad de asientos ocupados después de una compra.
- Ajuste del tamaño de la columna `numberFlight` y de sus relaciones para soportar el nuevo formato de identificador de vuelo.
- Modificación de la lógica para permitir validar vuelos que aún no existen físicamente en la tabla `Flight`.

## Backend
- Creación del DTO `CheckFlightAvailabilityDto`.
- Implementación del método `CheckFlightAvailabilityAsync` en Repository, Service e Interfaces correspondientes.
- Creación del endpoint `POST /api/payment/check-availability`.
- Integración de la validación de disponibilidad mediante Stored Procedures.
- Actualización de la lógica de creación automática de vuelos para inicializar correctamente los campos de ocupación.
- Integración de la reserva automática de asientos al confirmar una compra.
- Corrección y validación del flujo de creación de vuelos durante el proceso de compra.

## Frontend
- Implementación de validación de disponibilidad al presionar los botones de compra de vuelos.
- Implementación de una segunda validación de disponibilidad inmediatamente antes de procesar el pago.
- Soporte para vuelos directos y vuelos con escalas mediante validación individual de cada segmento.
- Integración de `PopupMessage` para mostrar errores de disponibilidad en lugar de alertas del navegador.
- Corrección de redireccionamientos y flujo de navegación cuando no existen campos disponibles.
- Ajustes para utilizar el formato correcto de número de vuelo durante las verificaciones.

# Resultado
- Se evita que un usuario continúe el proceso de compra cuando no existen campos disponibles.
- Se evita la sobreventa de asientos al realizar una segunda validación antes del pago.
- Se mantiene sincronizada la ocupación de asientos con las compras realizadas.
- Se soportan correctamente vuelos directos y vuelos con escalas.

author: detain
body:
## Phase 1 of the sugar-reel post-audit remediation

Resource-safety & lifecycle fixes — the latent hangs / silent-death issues, fixed first so later phases' smoke tests can't deadlock the terminal. No user-visible behavior change except "video no longer wedges."

### Fixes
- **F7 — ffmpeg stderr sink** (`FfmpegDecoder`): stderr was held open in a pipe and never read; on noisy/corrupt input ffmpeg blocks once the ~64KB kernel pipe buffer fills, which wedges our blocking `fread(stdout)` in `next()`. Redirected stderr to a `/dev/null` file sink; removed the `$stderr` property and its `close()` handling.
- **F8 — audio subprocess sinks** (`AudioPlayer`): `start()` opened stdin/stdout/stderr as pipes then immediately `fclose()`d them; ffplay/mpv writing a status line to the now-reader-less stderr pipe can take SIGPIPE and die → audio silently stops. Switched to `/dev/null` file sinks (no parent-side pipes to race); dropped the dead `=== 0` `proc_open` guard.
- **F9 — end-of-stream handling + optional loop** (`Player`, `Reel`): an exhausted decoder used to keep the last frame and reschedule ticks forever (an fps busy-loop, no quit/indicator). Added `Player::$ended`/`$loop`; on exhaustion the player either stops ticking cleanly with an `[ended]  0 restart  q quit` status line (non-loop) or wraps to frame 0 — recreating the decoder and restarting audio from t0 (loop, via new `Reel::withLoop()`). A seek out of the ended state clears it and re-arms the tick chain.

### Notes
- Incremental ordering: this phase predates `rebuildDecoderAt()` (Phase 2) and the `elapsed`→`videoTime` rename (Phase 3), so the loop restart uses an inline rebuild with the existing `/fake` test-path guard and keeps the `elapsed` field — Phase 2 folds it into the shared helper.
- F7/F8 live tests are watchdog-guarded characterisation tests: a real subprocess-hang repro is itself a hazard, so they prove the structural guarantees (no held stderr pipe; clean spawn → running → stop → no-orphan lifecycle) rather than flipping a hang on/off.

## Test plan
`cd sugar-reel && vendor/bin/phpunit` → **177 passing / 4 skipped** (was 169/4; +8 tests). The 4 skips are the binary-*absent* tests, which skip because ffmpeg/ffplay are present on this host. The F9 regression tests (`testExhaustedDecoderStopsTickingWhenNotLooping`, `testLoopWrapsToFrameZeroAndKeepsTicking`) were verified to fail on the un-fixed code and pass after the fix. `php tools/check-path-repos.php` → closure clean (no wiring changed). Live subprocess tests are watchdog-guarded; no ffplay/ffmpeg orphans after the run.

author: guerrinflorian
body:
## Summary
- Fix appliqué dans les bons fichiers : `src/pages/` (Nuxt route les pages depuis ce dossier, pas `src/views/`)
- Le commit précédent corrigeait `src/views/` par erreur — aucun effet en production

## Cause technique
Vue 2 appelle `updateClass()` sur tous les éléments lors de chaque patch DOM. Cette fonction écrase l'attribut `class` avec la valeur du vnode statique, supprimant `animate-in` ajouté manuellement. Le carrousel retrouvait alors `opacity: 0` avec une transition CSS de ~0.9s.

## Solution (appliquée sur naissance, famille, grossesse, portrait)
- `created()` : initialise `_animatedElements` comme propriété d'instance non-réactive
- `updated()` : ré-applique `animate-in` à chaque élément animé après chaque patch Vue (s'exécute dans le même microtask que le patch, donc invisible pour le browser)
- `setupScrollObserver` : stocke les éléments animés dans `_animatedElements`
- `beforeDestroy()` : nettoie l'observer

author: davmont
body:
## Summary

Three small changes that together get \`top(1)\` running cleanly on the post-Tier-1 amd64 iso, plus an in-tree warning so future contributors don't accidentally repeat the struct-proc binary-ABI mistake that surfaced via PR #158.

## 1. top: accept amd64/x86_64 as synonyms (\`external/bsd/top/dist/top.c\`)

\`top\` was built with \`UNAME_HARDWARE=\"amd64\"\` (from \`\${MACHINE}\` in the Makefile) but PM's \`uname(2)\` returns \`\"x86_64\"\` (the \`MACHINE_ARCH\` value).  The strict \`strcmp\` rejected the running kernel as \"incompatible hardware platform\" and exited.

Extend the check with a small alias table so \`amd64\` ↔ \`x86_64\` and \`i386\` ↔ \`i686\` are treated as the same architecture.  Defensive: any future port that hits the same MACHINE vs MACHINE_ARCH split is covered too.

## 2. kernel: \`get_cpu_ticks\` divide-by-zero guard (\`arch/x86_64/arch_clock.c\`)

With #1 fixed, \`top\` proceeds to its real work and immediately triggers a **kernel divide-by-zero panic** in \`get_cpu_ticks\`:

\`\`\`c
ticks[i] = tsc_per_state[cpu][i] / tsc_per_tick[cpu];
\`\`\`

\`tsc_per_tick[cpu]\` is populated when \`init_local_timer()\` runs on that CPU.  For a CPU number that exists in the config (\`cpu < CONFIG_MAX_CPUS\` — the only check \`do_getinfo\`'s \`GET_CPUTICKS\` makes) but is past \`ncpus\` or was never timer-initialised, the value is still zero.  \`top\` iterates over \`CONFIG_MAX_CPUS\` in its \`sysctl(kern.cp_times)\` call and lands exactly on an uninitialised slot.

Fix: return zeros for uninitialised CPUs.

## 3. kernel/proc.h: document the struct proc binary-ABI constraint

The Tier 1 colocation work (PR #157) added a per-CPU histogram inside \`struct proc\`, growing its size by 128 bytes per slot.  Several userspace servers (MIB, IS, VM) copy the kernel proc table verbatim via \`GET_PROCTAB\` into a locally-typed \`struct proc proc_tab[NR_TASKS+NR_PROCS]\` buffer.  Stale binaries vs new kernel → buffer overrun → \`ps\` crashes — which is what PR #158 fixed by moving the field back out.

Add a prominent warning at the top of \`struct proc\` explaining the constraint and pointing future contributors at the \`ipc_sender_cpu_count[][]\` pattern in \`proc.c\` as the canonical example of how to add per-proc kernel-internal state without touching the struct.

## Verification (-smp 4 iso)

\`\`\`
# top -b -n 1
load averages:  0.92,  0.49,  0.16;               up 0+00:02:48        09:12:54
36 processes: 1 runnable, 35 sleeping
CPU states:  0.0% user,  0.0% nice,  6.2% system,  6.2% kernel,  0.0% idle
Memory: 255M Total, 180M Free, 180M Contig, 472K Cached

  PID USERNAME PRI NICE   SIZE   RES STATE      TIME   WCPU    CPU COMMAND
    0 root       0    0    13M   13M kernel/0   0:00  7.48%  7.47% [kernel]
\`\`\`

- Before #1: \`top\` exits with \"incompatible hardware platform\"
- After #1 alone: kernel panic in \`get_cpu_ticks\` (divide error)
- After #1 + #2: full output as above
- \`ps -el\` continues to work (PR #159 unaffected)
- \`ipcbench\` p50 ~16k on -smp 4 (Tier 1 unaffected)

author: ldnvnbl
body:
## Summary

Implements the design in `docs/db-backed-execution-scheduler-rfc.md` (review PR #3701) to remove the hard `pg_cron` dependency from the `task_usage_hourly` rollup pipeline. Self-host installs no longer need `cron.schedule(...)`, multi-instance deployments get a per-`(job, scope, plan_time)` lease, and the v0.3.4 → current direct-upgrade path no longer trips migration 103's fail-closed guard.

## What's in this PR

- `migrations/113_sys_cron_executions`: distributed lease + audit table. Unique key `(job_name, scope_kind, scope_id, plan_time)`, `status TEXT + CHECK`, `lease_token` rotated on every claim/steal, partial indexes for stale RUNNING / recent FAILED / retention.
- `internal/taskusagebackfill`: idempotent monthly-slice backfill of `task_usage_hourly` under advisory lock `4246`. Exposes `Hook()` invoked by `cmd/migrate up` immediately before migration 103, so a v0.3.4 jump does not require the operator to run `cmd/backfill_task_usage_hourly` by hand. Watermark is stamped from the DB's own clock (`now() - INTERVAL '5 minutes'`) so a clock-skewed app process cannot stamp it into the DB's future.
- `internal/scheduler`: thin shell around the SQL primitives.
  - `tryClaim` does `INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` then a stale-steal/retry `UPDATE` in a single round-trip.
  - `heartbeat`, `finishSuccess`, `finishFailure` all match on `(id, lease_token, status='RUNNING')` so an ex-lease-holder cannot overwrite a newer attempt's terminal state.
  - `Manager` drives `latest_only` and `every_plan` catch-up; per-handler `RunTimeout` ctx with a detached background heartbeat goroutine.
  - Manager always sweeps abandoned RUNNING leases (regardless of `AllowStaleReentry`) so `latest_only` jobs do not strand a stuck row indefinitely; reentrant retries are still served via the `tryClaim` retry-from-FAILED branch.
  - Handler panics are surfaced through a named-return recover into `finishFailure` with `error_code='handler_panic'`.
- `internal/scheduler/jobs_task_usage`: registers `rollup_task_usage_hourly` per RFC §11.1 (5m cadence, latest_only, allow_stale_reentry, 25m run_timeout / 30m stale_timeout, 1m/5m/15m backoff). Handler calls `SELECT rollup_task_usage_hourly()` — the SQL function still holds advisory lock `4246` internally, so a leftover `pg_cron` tick or manual call cannot double-write.
- `cmd/server/main.go`: registers the manager under `sweepCtx` so it shuts down with the other background workers. The skip path is "manager logs the error on the failing tick and retries on the next cycle" — registration failure (e.g. duplicate name) is the only fatal case at startup.
- Docs (English + ja / ko / zh): self-host quickstart §7 demotes `pg_cron` to a compatibility note; troubleshooting "Usage dashboard stays at zero" + migration 103 sections updated; `SELF_HOSTING_ADVANCED.md → Usage Dashboard Rollup` rewritten to lead with the in-process scheduler.

## Tests

Cover the four RFC §14 rows张大彪 called out and the three additional follow-ups Eve flagged on review:

- `taskusagebackfill.TestHook_DirectV034Upgrade` — apply migrations through 102, seed `task_usage` 2h old, confirm migration 103 trips the guard, run `Hook()`, confirm 103 then applies cleanly.
- `taskusagebackfill.TestHook_FreshDatabaseStampsWatermarkOnly` — empty DB path: watermark stamped, 103 passes via its fresh-DB branch.
- `scheduler.TestStaleStealTerminalUpdateIgnored` — claim → force `stale_after` into the past → second runner steals (rotates lease_token, increments attempt) → first runner's `finishSuccess` returns `ErrLeaseLost` → row stays in second runner's RUNNING state → second runner's `finishSuccess` succeeds with its rows_affected.
- `scheduler.TestConcurrentClaimsSingleWinner` — 8 concurrent contenders against the same plan_time, exactly 1 `Won`, 7 `Conflicted`, 0 `Stole`, 1 row in DB matches winner.
- `scheduler.TestPgCronConcurrentNoDoubleWrite` — 6 goroutines call `SELECT rollup_task_usage_hourly()` directly while watermark is forced backwards; advisory lock 4246 admits exactly one writer and the post-rollup `task_usage_hourly` matches the seeded fixture.
- `scheduler.TestManagerTickClosesAbandonedRunning` — drives `Manager.runOnce` end-to-end for both reentrant true/false; old stale row becomes FAILED + `error_code='stale_timeout'`, current plan claimed and finishes SUCCESS.
- `scheduler.TestManagerHandlerPanicWritesFailed` — panicking handler ends up FAILED + `error_code='handler_panic'`, NOT silently SUCCESS.
- `scheduler.TestManagerEveryPlanRetriesFailedSamePlanTime` — every_plan job whose handler always errors: tick 1 leaves FAILED+attempt=1+next_retry_at, force next_retry_at into past, tick 2 retries the SAME plan_time at attempt=2 (does not skip to plan+cadence).
- `scheduler.TestFloorPlanUTC` — UTC bucket math unit test.

Local results against the bundled `pgvector/pgvector:pg17`:

```
ok    github.com/multica-ai/multica/server/internal/scheduler           ~0.8s
ok    github.com/multica-ai/multica/server/internal/taskusagebackfill   ~1.5s
```

`go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` both clean across the affected packages.

## Out of scope (tracked separately)

The original RFC includes two operational-hardening pieces that are deliberately not in this PR; they do not block the `pg_cron` migration and are tracked in [MUL-3076](mention://issue/5f514124-b3a5-4bb6-b9d1-8215fd6a081f):

- **RFC §10 — Observability metrics.** The audit table `sys_cron_executions` is queryable directly with the indexes shipped in migration 113. The RFC's metric surface (`scheduler_claim_total`, `scheduler_plan_lag_seconds`, `scheduler_running_stale_total`, etc.) and the alert rules that consume them will land as a follow-up so this PR stays focused.
- **RFC §10.4 — Retention prune.** `prune_sys_cron_executions` is not registered yet. Steady-state row count is bounded but not actively reaped; cluster runs correctly without it, and the prune job itself will run through this same scheduler once it lands.

## Migration / rollback notes

- Migration 113 is forward-only at the schema level; the rollback drops `sys_cron_executions`, which is only an audit table — no business data lives there.
- If this PR is reverted but migration 113 has already applied, the table can stay in place untouched.
- Existing operators with a registered `pg_cron` job for `rollup_task_usage_hourly` need not unschedule it — the SQL function still uses advisory lock 4246, so the app scheduler and `pg_cron` cannot double-write. The unschedule SQL is in the docs as a cleanup step.

Closes [MUL-2957](mention://issue/56f3b8ee-e930-4485-a253-a7026f3cdd5e). Design RFC: #3701. Follow-up: [MUL-3076](mention://issue/5f514124-b3a5-4bb6-b9d1-8215fd6a081f).

author: chaowao
body:
## Summary

The remaining two reasons the nightly **ASAN/UBSan** sim cell is red (the `asan`
preset is `address,undefined`, so it also runs UBSan). With #979 (Callable
alignment), these were the only two UBSan findings on `prepared_callable`.

### 1. Signed-overflow at scheduler boot (real UB)
`SchedulerContext::init` sums every ring's `current_task_index` to seed
`total_tasks_`. It runs at one-time AICPU boot — **before** the SM is reset for
the run (`aicpu_executor` SM init) — so a ring not yet written holds
uninitialized memory. Under ASAN's malloc-fill that's `0xbebebebe`, a **negative
int32**, and the int32 accumulation overflows → UBSan `signed-integer-overflow`.

Fix: accumulate in `int64_t` and skip non-positive rings. Uninitialized/garbage
rings now contribute 0 (the correct boot count, since no tasks are submitted
yet) and valid counts still add up, with no overflow. Applied to a2a3 and a5.

### 2. Scope ASAN off the L3 oversubscription hang
The a2a3 ASAN cell timed out (124) — `dynamic_register` is **all `level=3`**
chip-fork cases, which livelock on the 4-vCPU runner under a sanitizer's
slowdown (#884 oversubscription family). This is exactly why TSAN is scoped to
`prepared_callable`; ASAN now does the same. UBSan stays `halt_on_error=1`, so
it remains a **real gate** on any undefined behaviour.

## Validation
- Both UBSan findings on `prepared_callable` were enumerated (11 misaligned +
  1 overflow); #979 fixes the first, this fixes the second — none remain.
- Scheduler change compiles cleanly (local sim rebuild).
- End-to-end (sim ASAN/UBSan cell + onboard) is validated by CI / the next
  nightly. Needs **#979 merged too** for the cell to be fully green.

## Testing
- [x] Local sim build passes with the change
- [ ] Next nightly: ASAN/UBSan cell green (with #979)

body:
Automated task execution for `T01` via codex.

**Task Context:**
## Objective
Extend the onboarding Git step (step id `"git"`) with a Remote/Local mode toggle. In Local mode, hide the GitHub and GitLab SectionCards and show only the Git identity card plus an info banner explaining that automatic CI and pull requests will not work and that Remote mode is recommended.

## Scope
- `src/contracts/app-types.ts` — `CliWorkflowConfig` interface (line ~748)
- `src/repositories/settings-defaults.ts` — `DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_SETTINGS.cliWorkflow` object
- `src/domain/settings/settings-sanitizers/cli-workflow-sanitizer.ts` — `sanitizeCliWorkflow()` return object
- `dashboard/src/v2/components/onboarding/OnboardingExperience.tsx` — git step block (lines 1142–1209)

## Implementation Requirements
1. Add `gitMode: "remote" | "local"` to the `CliWorkflowConfig` interface in `src/contracts/app-types.ts`.
2. Add `gitMode: "remote"` as the default in `DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_SETTINGS.cliWorkflow` in `src/repositories/settings-defaults.ts`.
3. Add `gitMode: readString(cliInput.gitMode, DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_SETTINGS.cliWorkflow.gitMode) as "remote" | "local"` (with a fallback guard to `"remote"` for invalid values) to the `sanitizeCliWorkflow()` return object in `cli-workflow-sanitizer.ts`.
4. In `OnboardingExperience.tsx`, at the top of the `active.id === "git"` block (just before the first `<div data-onboarding-card>`), add a Remote/Local toggle using the same pill-button pattern already used for source type toggles elsewhere. Read from `settings.defaults.cliWorkflow.gitMode` and write via `updateCliWorkflow({ gitMode: ... })`.
5. Wrap the GitHub `SectionCard` block (lines 1144–1168) and the GitLab `SectionCard` block (lines 1169–1179) in `{settings.defaults.cliWorkflow.gitMode !== "local" && (...)}` so they are hidden when Local is selected.
6. Below the toggle (and above the Git identity card), when `gitMode === "local"`, render an info banner using the `Info` icon from lucide-preact with the text: "Local mode does not support automatic CI or pull requests. Remote mode is recommended for full feature access."

## Constraints
- Do not alter the Git identity SectionCard (lines 1180–1208) — it must remain visible in both modes.
- The toggle must persist across onboarding sessions via the existing `updateCliWorkflow()` mechanism — no separate local React state for gitMode.
- Do not break the schema validation: if the saved value is anything other than `"remote"` or `"local"`, the sanitizer must fall back to `"remote"`.
- Keep the info banner visually consistent with the existing onboarding card styling (rounded border, muted background).

## Verification
- Run `npm run typecheck` — zero TypeScript errors.
- Run `npm test` — all tests pass.
- In the onboarding UI, navigate to the Git step (step 2/4): toggle should appear at the top. Selecting Local hides GitHub and GitLab cards and shows the info banner. Selecting Remote restores GitHub and GitLab cards and hides the banner. Git identity card is visible in both modes.

**Sprint Context:**
Add Remote/Local git mode selection to onboarding step 2/4 with conditional GitHub/GitLab hiding and a Local-mode info warning; embed New Project creation into AddProjectModal as a 'NEW PROJECT' source type that hides the Setup Agent and shows init-mode buttons; fix relative project paths to resolve against the user home directory.

Bumps the Android Gradle Plugin, Kotlin Gradle plugins, Compose BOM, and three
libraries to current versions, and regenerates the SHA-256 dependency-verification
metadata so the reproducible build keeps passing. App version is unchanged (v0.9.0).

Supersedes the 5 open Dependabot PRs, whose pipelines failed: each bumped a single
dependency without regenerating `gradle/verification-metadata.xml`, so Gradle's
`verify-metadata` rejected the new artifacts before tests could run. This PR bumps
all of them together (plus the coupled compose plugin) and refreshes the pins.

## Related Issue

Supersedes/closes Dependabot PRs:
- `com.android.application` 9.2.1
- `org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.serialization` 2.3.21
- `org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-serialization-json` 1.11.0

- `org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.compose` 2.2.10 → 2.3.21 *(forced lockstep — both Kotlin Gradle plugins must share 
one version, else the build fails on a plugin version mismatch)*

platform sites)

- Documented under v0.9.0 in `CHANGELOG.md` and the fastlane `12.txt` changelogs (en/de, under F-Droid's 500-char
limit)

author: ilhan007
body:
Follow-up to #13604.

Replaces `secrets.UI5_WEBCOMP_BOT_GH_TOKEN` with a per-run installation token from `actions/create-github-app-token@v3.2.0` (pinned by SHA) in the four workflows that were intentionally left out of scope when the release workflow was migrated:

- `deploy-preview.yaml`
- `reset-preview-deploy.yaml`
- `reset-gh-pages.yaml`
- `issue-monthly-report.yaml`

## Why

Completes the [OSPO Hardening Control #4](https://wiki.one.int.sap/wiki/spaces/ospodocs/pages/6139514269/GitHub+Hardening+Controls#GitHubHardeningControls-4.Replacelong-livedsecretswithOIDC) migration: replace long-lived static credentials (PATs) with short-lived per-workflow tokens. App tokens are valid for ~1 hour and disappear when the run ends, drastically reducing the blast radius compared to the long-lived PAT.

## After merge

Once each workflow has run green at least once, the `UI5_WEBCOMP_BOT_GH_TOKEN` secret can be deleted and the underlying PAT revoked.

`UI5_WEBCOMP_BOT_NAME` and `UI5_WEBCOMP_BOT_EMAIL` are kept — they are git identity strings, not credentials.

## Required (already in place from #13604)

- `RELEASE_APP_ID` repo secret
- `RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` repo secret
- The `sap-ui5-webcomponents-release` GitHub App installed on this repo (only needs Contents/Issues/PRs write — no branch protection bypass changes required, since none of these workflows push to `main`)

author: binaricat
body:
## Background

This is the Google Drive counterpart to #1208, which fixed OneDrive access-token refresh persistence. `GoogleDriveAdapter` had the same gap: refreshed access tokens were stored only in memory and were not persisted, so the next app launch could load an expired token and force the user to authorize again.

Refs #1189

## Changes

- Adds `setOnTokensRefreshed(callback)` to `GoogleDriveAdapter`.
- Adds a shared `refreshTokens()` helper so `setTokens` and `ensureValidToken` both update memory and trigger persistence.
- Clears the refresh callback on `signOut()`.
- Preserves the previous Google refresh token when a refresh response omits a new one, matching Google OAuth behavior.
- Updates comments around token refresh persistence to include Google.

## Out of Scope

This PR does not generalize OneDrive's reauth-required marker flow to Google. That would require a broader cross-layer refactor and is left for follow-up work.

## Tests

- Adds `GoogleDriveAdapter.test.ts` for refreshed-token persistence, refresh-token preservation, expired-token refresh, best-effort callbacks, and sign-out cleanup.
- Extends `persistRefreshedTokens.test.ts` with a real Google adapter path through `attachTokenRefreshPersistence`.

author: cyhhao
body:
## Lock the mobile app shell to the visual viewport (iOS keyboard)

On-device follow-up: the chat/home composer still flew **off the top of the screen** when focused on iOS Safari (my earlier layout-only changes didn't fix it).

### Root cause
The page is slightly taller than the screen (the mobile header sits on top of a `min-h-screen` `main`), so the document **can scroll**. iOS then scrolls the whole document to "reveal" the focused input and overshoots, pushing it above the viewport. Removing `interactive-widget` / top-aligning the home didn't help because the document could still scroll.

### Fix (Telegram / PWA-shell pattern)
On **mobile only**: lock the document (`html,body { overflow:hidden; height:100% }`) and make `AppShell` a fixed, `--app-vvh`-sized flex column — `header` (`shrink-0`) + `main` (`flex-1 overflow-y-auto`) that scrolls **internally**. With nowhere for the document to scroll, iOS can't fling the input off the top; and because the shell is sized to the visual viewport (via `useViewportHeightVar`), it shrinks with the keyboard so the composer stays flush above it. **Desktop is unchanged** (`md:` keeps `min-h-screen` + normal document flow).

### Evidence
- Build green; `npm run validate:theme` passes.
- ⚠️ **Must be verified on a real iOS device** — I can't run iOS Safari in my environment, and this is a layout-level change. Please test: home `/` + a chat, focus the input → it should sit above the keyboard, not jump off the top; and confirm admin/settings long pages still scroll and desktop is unaffected.

### Risk / blast radius
This changes the mobile scroll model (document → internal `main` scroll). Desktop is gated behind `md:`. Long mobile pages (admin/settings) now scroll within `main`. Possible follow-up: a minor safe-area-top scroll on notch devices in the chat (the chat keeps its `--app-vvh - 4rem` height).

author: bborbe
body:
## Summary

Production pr-reviewer-agent pod was logging `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` and `GH_TOKEN` to stdout via `glog.V(2).Infof("cmd.Env = %+v", cmd.Env)` in `lib/claude/claude-runner.go:117` and a sibling V(4) line in `lib/pi/pi-runner.go:117`. Confirmed in prod logs of `pr-reviewer-agent-6ef56a8f-20260603055105-jr6cf` on 2026-06-03 — any operator with cluster log access could read both tokens.

This change adds a shared `envparse.RedactForLog([]string) []string` helper that replaces values for sensitive keys with the literal `***`. Keys stay visible (operators still see *which* vars are passed), only values are masked. Match is case-insensitive substring against `TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `PASSWORD`, `PASSWD`, `CREDENTIAL`, `API_KEY`, `PRIVATE_KEY`, `ACCESS_KEY`. Wired into both log sites. Nil-safe (returns nil for nil so `cmd.Env` inherit-parent semantics survive). Non-mutating (callers reuse `cmd.Env` for the real subprocess).

`lib/envparse` test coverage: 100%.

## Test plan

- [x] `make precommit` passes in `lib/`
- [x] 28 Ginkgo cases in `lib/envparse` (case-insensitive positives, allow-list negatives, ordering, no-`=` passthrough, empty sensitive value, non-mutation, nil-in → nil-out)
