author: bandarudheeraj
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3198.

When a caller propagates `session.id` via OTel baggage (e.g. Langfuse's
`propagate_attributes(session_id=..., as_baggage=True)`), a `SpanProcessor`
can write that value on `span.on_start`. However `_extract_init_attributes`
and `_extract_usage_and_cost_attributes` both unconditionally set `SESSION_ID`
from the Claude CLI's internal session UUID mid-stream, overwriting the
application-provided value and breaking trace correlation in Langfuse.

**Root cause:** two unconditional `attributes[SESSION_ID] = session_id` writes
in `_wrappers.py` — one in `_extract_init_attributes` (system init message)
and one in `_extract_usage_and_cost_attributes` (result message).

**Fix:** add a `_baggage_has_session_id()` guard that checks current OTel
baggage before each write. If `session.id` is already in baggage the
instrumentation skips its write, deferring to whatever the SpanProcessor set
on `on_start`. For callers not using baggage the behaviour is unchanged — the
Claude internal UUID is still recorded.

## Test plan

- New regression test `test_session_id_not_overwritten_by_claude_internal_uuid`
  in `test_instrumentor.py` that:
  - Sets `session.id` in OTel baggage (simulating `propagate_attributes`)
  - Wires a Langfuse-style `SpanProcessor` that writes baggage → span on start
  - Replays an existing cassette (no API key needed)
  - Asserts the exported span retains the application session ID, not the Claude UUID
- Test **fails** before this fix and **passes** after (verified in CI)

## Alternatives considered

- **Rename** Claude's session to `claude.session_id` — breaking change, rejected
- **Check span attribute before writing** — no reliable `span.get_attribute()` in public OTel API
- **Only write on init message** — still races with `on_start` processors

# Pull Request: Improve chunking strategy for long legal documents

## Closes #846

## Summary
The current chunker splits on blank lines (paragraphs), but statutory sections in real documents are often separated by a single newline, so two sections could land in one chunk and dilute embedding retrieval. Thus, this PR improves the chunking strategy for long legal documents by adding section-aware splitting on top of the current paragraph/sentence packing. 

## What's in this PR
- New `split_legal_sections()` that breaks a document at section headings - `Section`/`Sec.`/`S.`, `Article`/`Art.`, the `§` symbol, and `(Order N) Rule N` - even when not separated by a blank line. Preamble before the first heading is kept as its own block.
- `chunk_text()` gains `respect_sections: bool = True`: it chunks each section independently so **no chunk straddles two sections** and every chunk is anchored to its provision. Overlap context never crosses a section boundary.
- Setting `respect_sections=False` restores the previous paragraph-only behaviour exactly (backwards compatible).

body:
## What & why

Replaces BAL-247's placeholder rail with the production **Search Composer** for Expert Search ([BAL-249](https://linear.app/balo-tech/issue/BAL-249)). The composer is not "a bar" or "a rail" — it is one `SearchFilters` state (serialized to the URL) plus controls that read/write it, rendered across three surfaces that **cannot drift** because they all bind to the same URL state. It produces filters into the contract that the results page (BAL-247) hydrates and the search API (BAL-246) consumes — **no change to the search contract**.

## Surfaces

- **UnifiedBar** — hero (tall, centered, gradient hero) + compact (persists on results) variants. Segmented FTS + Product/Support/When popovers; segments summarise active state inline.
- **FacetControls** — **one** component shared by the desktop rail (`hidden md:block`) and the mobile bottom sheet (committed vs pending modes): products, type-of-help, availability, rate (dual-handle), languages.
- **ProductSelector** — the centerpiece: **one** search-first component (search box → selected-tokens tray → grouped chips, dense groups cap to 4 + "+N more") mounted **three ways** via `collapsible`/`inSheet` (bar popover, collapsible rail, in-sheet).
- **MobileComposerBar** — single **one-trigger** collapsed bar (active-filter summary + count) opening the full sheet with the sticky "Show N experts" footer.

## Key implementation notes

- **Taxonomy** loaded server-side (RSC) via `referenceDataRepository.getSkillsByVertical` (repo-direct, no new endpoint), with id→name mapping for display **and** analytics. `products[]` carry skill UUIDs; "Industries" is a skill-category that writes `products[]` — deliberately **not** wired to the API's separate `industries[]` filter.
- **Firing model** (`use-facet-requery`): FTS always explicit-submit (never per-keystroke); facet changes live-requery **debounced ~500ms**, gated on results-present. Hero composes intent with no requery.
- **Rate** binds to `rateMinDollars`/`rateMaxDollars` (A$); cents conversion stays at the API boundary. "Any time" → `timeframe: null`.
- **Analytics** (extends `SEARCH_EVENTS`): `search_submitted` (with the derived first-class `path` = query_only|facets_only|both|none), `search_refined`, plus `product_selector_opened`/`searched`, `product_group_expanded`, `composer_cleared`. Logs `query_length`, **never** query text.
- **Motion** polish (chip tap-scale, token layout reflow, collapse/reveal) gated on `useReducedMotion`.
- **No schema changes.**

## Process (multi-agent /implement)

Resolver pre-flight → architect plan → build → **UX ✅ / Security ✅ / Review ✅** (one fix-loop: removed a duplicate mobile filter trigger and wired three previously-dead analytics events) → pre-PR gate **GREEN**.

## Testing

- New unit tests: taxonomy id↔name mapping, the analytics `path` derivation + snapshot builder, the `use-facet-requery` debounce/results-gate.
- New component tests (RTL): ProductSelector, UnifiedBar, FacetControls, MobileComposerBar, SearchComposer + leaf atoms; updated `filter-sheet` / `results-controls` / `results-toolbar` / page tests.
- Full monorepo suite green under UTC (CI env); typecheck, lint, build, format all pass. SonarCloud new-code coverage ≥80% on every changed production file. No DB/repository changes → no integration tests in scope.

Closes BAL-249.

## What

Two related changes for getting **on-demand** NMEA 2000 data — data a device only sends when asked — and decoding the route messages a Garmin chartplotter emits.

### 1. `feat(pgn)`: Garmin 126720 route navigation decoders
A GPSMAP broadcasts its active route over two proprietary 126720 sub-types (independent of autopilot engagement). Decoded and registered onto `Registry[126720]` via `init()` (the `ac_utility.go` hand-written-helper pattern), so every consumer gets them automatically (`lplex dump --decode`, `/events?decode=true`, `/history`, the Go `pgn` package):
- `(0x61,0x06)` **GarminActiveWaypoint** — next waypoint + distance + ETA
- `(0x12,0x07)` **GarminDestinationNav** — final destination + distance + ETA + id

Fields validated against a full day of real GPSMAP frames (distances count down to match boat→waypoint range; ETAs match arrival times; positions step through the route). Validated packet-test vectors included.

### 2. `feat`: declarative on-demand request rules (`requestrules` package)
Some data isn't broadcast — the device only sends it on request (product info, the Route & Waypoint service, Victron on-demand registers, anything on-demand). Rather than bespoke request code per case, this adds one **declarative engine**:

> When a device matching `<vendor/model/class/NAME/…>` comes online (or at startup), request `<data>`; keep it fresh (`max-age`); re-request when `<trigger PGN>` is seen — never faster than `min-interval`.

```hocon
requests = [
  { name = "gpsmap-route", match { model-id = "GPSMAP*" }, via = "iso",
    want = [130065, 130067], to-device = true, on-online = true,
    max-age = "30s", min-interval = "5s", invalidate-on = [129284] }
]
```

**Key properties**
- **Level-triggered** (request only while missing/stale, never on every event) + a required **per-target `min-interval` floor** and optional **global floor** → the bus is never flooded, however many triggers fire.
- Matching by manufacturer / manufacturer-code / model-id (glob) / device-class / device-function / NAME / source / bus.
- `via = "iso"` (ISO Request) **and** `via = "frame"` (parameterized, sub-keyed frames, e.g. Victron register reads — frame template user-supplied).
- Surfaces: **HOCON** (`requests = [...]`, `requests-global-min-interval`) **and Go API** (`BrokerConfig.RequestRules`, `Broker.AddRequestRule`).
- Transport-agnostic core (no import of root `lplex`); disabled in replica mode; bypasses `/send` policy like the broker's built-in discovery.

**Broker integration** is hot-path-safe: a lock-free `InterestingPGNs()` set means the per-frame cost is one map lookup; engine hooks fire only at device discovery/eviction and for relevant frames, plus a 10 s tick for refresh.

## Tests
- `requestrules`: 11 unit tests (matching, min-interval floor, max-age refresh, sub-keyed frames, global floor, offline reset, unknown-device guard) with an injectable clock.
- Broker: end-to-end test that a discovered device triggers the configured ISO request.
- Config: HOCON parsing of both ISO and frame rules + required-field validation.
- `go build ./...`, full `go test ./...`, `golangci-lint run` — all green.

## Notes
- The Victron register **read-request frame format** isn't yet validated against a live device; the `via = "frame"` mechanism is general and the template is config-supplied, so it's ready once that format is confirmed.
- Built-in product-info discovery isn't yet migrated to a default rule (kept as-is to limit blast radius); easy follow-up.

The **last moogafakkin module** — this completes the full Moog System 55 + 35 clone line. 🎚️

## What
A horizontal **touch-ribbon**: press + slide along the strip to set a continuous **pitch CV**, with a **GATE** that goes HIGH while touched.

## Summary

Fixes 3 harvest regressions surfaced by **run 26899131808** (Factory 1/4, sha `6bc10506`). A fresh 1/4 harvest validated the HuggingFace hang-fix (HF **SUCCESS**), but **Academic + Ecosystem FAILED**. Diagnosis + fixes below.

### Run 26899131808 diagnosis
1. **ArXiv 60min false-timeout** — ArXiv step hit its `timeout-minutes: 60` cap while HEALTHY (ingested 16200, Failed 0, still progressing). Its 100K target + OAI 20s/page pagination legitimately needs ~140min+.
2. **LangChain #2116 manifest 30s×N stall** — `fetchManifestBody`'s 429 path did a silent flat `await delay(30000); return null` per prompt. A rate-limiting hub × ~100 items = ~50min → whole LangChain harvest timed out.
3. **Agents `_category` null** — `agents-adapter.js` could throw "Cannot set properties of null (setting '_category')" when a GitHub secondary-rate-limit returned null; caught/non-fatal today but silently dropped agent results.

---

### FIX 1 — ArXiv per-step timeout right-size
`.github/workflows/factory-harvest.yml`: raised the **Harvest ArXiv Papers** step `timeout-minutes` **60 → 180**. Kept (not removed) for hung-source protection; still under the 300min academic job-level cap (untouched). Other academic/ecosystem steps target far smaller sets (HF Papers 5K, HF Datasets 10K, S2 3K) and finish well inside 60min — left right-sized.

| step | before | after |
|------|--------|-------|
| Harvest ArXiv Papers | 60 | **180** |
| (all other per-step caps) | 60 | unchanged |
| academic job-level | 300 | unchanged |

### FIX 2 — LangChain manifest-enrichment aggregate stall (#2116)
- **(a) Aggregate circuit-breaker**: new run-scoped `ManifestEnricher` (in `langchain-manifest.js`) tracks CONSECUTIVE manifest-fetch failures across batches within one harvest run. After **8** consecutive failures it disables enrichment for the rest of the run (logged once: "manifest enrichment disabled after N consecutive failures — falling back to description"); all remaining items fall back to `description`. A success resets the counter. (Extracted to the manifest module to keep `langchain-adapter.js` ≤250 lines per CES.)
- **(b) Dropped the 30s flat 429 delay** in `fetchManifestBody` — on 429 / any non-OK, returns `null` immediately. The existing 6s AbortController still bounds a single hung fetch; the breaker handles persistence.
- Kept: 6s AbortController, honest description fallback, 500ms per-item pacing.

### FIX 3 — Agents `_category` null guard
`scripts/ingestion/adapters/agents-adapter.js`: explicit null-guards BEFORE setting `_category`, in both paths:
- **Curated**: `if (!data) { log + skip } else { data._category = cat; ... }`
- **Search**: drop null/unnamed items before the `forEach` sets `r._category`, and log the dropped count.

A null result is now skipped cleanly (and logged, not silently dropped), not crashed-and-caught.

---

### Verification
- **CES** (`scripts/check_compliance.py`): touched files pass — `langchain-adapter.js` 250, `langchain-manifest.js` 168, `agents-adapter.js` 229. (Only pre-existing untracked `*_tmp.html` trip CES; not part of this PR.)
- **actionlint**: OK on `factory-harvest.yml`.
- **node --check**: OK on all 3 JS files.
- **Node sanity**:
  - Fix 2: breaker disables after exactly 8 consecutive fails (fetch stops at 8 calls for 20 items), max delay 500ms (never 30000), all bodies fall back, elapsed ~2ms (no 30s stalls), counter resets on success. PASS.
  - Fix 3: null curated + null/unnamed search results skipped with logs, no throw, valid item survives. PASS.

author: diegohaz
body:
## Motivation

In the `website` workspace, not-found pages under the `/[category]/[page]` route returned HTTP `200` instead of `404`. For example:

```
GET https://ariakit.com/reference/this-api-does-not-exist-xyz → 200
```

This is a soft 404: the full layout renders with an empty main area, but the status code tells crawlers and tooling the page is valid.

The route at `website/app/(main)/[category]/[page]/page.tsx` already calls `notFound()` for unknown pages:

```tsx
const file = getFile(config, page);
if (!file) return notFound();
const content = getContent(config, file, page);
if (!content) return notFound();
```

But the route defaults to `dynamicParams = true`, so params that aren't generated by `generateStaticParams` are rendered on demand. During that on-demand render the `notFound()` is swallowed by the `@modal` parallel slot in `website/app/(main)/layout.tsx` (its `default.tsx` always resolves), so the response ends up a soft 404 with a `200` status. The single-segment route `(main)/[category]/page.tsx` was unaffected and already returned `404`.

## Solution

Opt the route out of on-demand rendering so unknown params return a real `404` at the routing layer, before the page (and the parallel slot) render:

```tsx
export const dynamicParams = false;
```

Every real page is already generated by `generateStaticParams` (confirmed on production: `dialog`, `use-dialog-store`, `dialog-provider`, etc. are all served as `PRERENDER`), so no valid page is affected — only unknown params now `404`.

## Verification

Ran the `website` dev server locally:

| URL | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/reference/dialog`, `/reference/use-dialog-store`, `/components/dialog`, `/examples/dialog`, `/guide/styling` | `200` | `200` |
| `/reference/this-api-does-not-exist-xyz` | `200` | `404` |
| `/components/…`, `/examples/…`, `/guide/…` (unknown) | `200` | `404` |
| `/nonexistentcategory/foo` | `200` | `404` |
| `/nonexistentcategory` (single segment) | `404` | `404` |

## Notes

- Scope is limited to the two-segment `[category]/[page]` route. Other dynamic routes already return `404` for unknown params (verified on production): the single-segment category route `/[category]` and the `/tags/[tag]` route both 404 correctly today, so they are intentionally left unchanged. The soft-404 only affects this route.
- No automated test is added: the legacy `website` Playwright harness does not discover any tests locally in this environment (its browser e2e is being migrated to the `app` workspace), so a regression test could not be authored and validated here. The fix was instead verified with the dev server (table above) against the confirmed production `200` baseline.

body:
# proposal-create

Generate polished, fully editable Arabic (RTL) proposal decks — automatically styled to any client's brand.

Point it at a website URL. It scans the CSS, extracts colors, typography, spacing, and assets, then outputs a ready-to-present `.pptx` file and a 9-slide component library — no Figma, no MCP, no manual brand work.


## What it does

- 🎨 **Brand scanner** — reads live CSS to extract color palette, font stack, border-radius, spacing scale
- 🖼 **Asset extractor** — downloads all site images, SVGs, icons, sprites, and fonts into organized folders
- 📐 **Component sheet** — generates a 9-slide PPTX library: palette, type scale, buttons, cards, dividers, grids, icons
- 📊 **Proposal builder** — builds a full Arabic RTL deck from a brief file + client URL
- 🔣 **Icon library** — site-extracted SVGs + Phosphor MIT fallback set, both embedded in PowerPoint as native shapes
- ✏️ **Fully editable** — every shape is a native PowerPoint object, no plugin or regen needed to adjust

author: simon-lm
body:
## What

Replaces the old French, partly **format-based** taxonomy (`Personnel/Documents`, `Banque`, `Personnel/Medias/Images|Videos|Audio`, `Revue_Manuelle`…) with a shallow, **English, context-first, subject-based** tree.

```text
Personal/
    Administrative/   Identity  Taxes  Banking  Insurance  Health  Housing  Telecom  Vehicle
    Education/
    Hobbies/
Work/
    Employment/   Administrative  Payslips
    Business/     Administrative  Invoices  Expenses  Clients
Manual_Review/
```

The AI still creates anything finer itself (`Clients/<name>`, `Insurance/Water-Damage-2025`, `Personal/Trip-Spain-2025`) — those are not part of the base tree.

## Why (the design rationale)

Decided over a long design discussion, driven by the project's mission (open-source, general-public, AI-driven, **accessibility / visually-impaired / ADHD**):

- **Context-first, admin nested in each context** — resolves the conceptual overlap (a tax doc is *both* administrative and personal) and the awkward naming it forced (no more "Administrative-perso" / "Personal-non-admin"). `Personal/Administrative` vs `Work/Administrative` disambiguate by nesting.
- **No format buckets** — classifying a photo as "media" because it's a `.jpg` is the same sin as `extension → folder`, one level up. A sinistre photo → its subject (Insurance evidence); a holiday photo → its event. The format only selects the reader.
- **Few top-level entries + a clear binary at each level** — fewer screen-reader nodes, less decision load (ADHD), predictable for the AI. Grounded in PIM research (navigation > search, shallow > deep, fit-to-user) — see the design memory.
- **Cross-cutting views** ("all my bills") come from the catalog fiche (keywords/entities) + soft-links, **not** by duplicating folders (Paperless-ngx pattern: folders for navigation, metadata for the rest).

## Code

- `taxonomy.BASE_LIBRARY_DIRECTORIES` rewritten; `INTERIM_LIBRARY_DIR` → `Manual_Review`.
- `existing_category_paths` de-duplicated (the tree is now nested, so a dir is reachable via several bases).
- All affected tests repointed to the new categories — **179 green**. Verified the 22 base dirs are created on a fresh layout.
- `README` + `docs/spec-mvp-v1.md §10` + `docs/backlog.md` (the Work-vs-Personal ambiguity is now the top-level binary) updated.

## Breaking (pre-release, never deployed)

Existing libraries with old French folders are **not** auto-migrated (sandbox users `reset`). The taxonomy is **hardcoded** for now — making it **user-editable** is a planned follow-up (and important for the accessibility mission: each user adapts it, the AI does the sorting).

## Next

This is chantier 1 of the agreed roadmap. Next: (2) EXIF dates + origin-folder in the fiche, then (3) the two-phase **catalog → organize** pipeline (Mistral medium, set-aware grouping by folder) that this taxonomy + the fiche enable.

author: eolaruhagen
body:
## What

Pass `near: -5000, far: 5000` to `withOrthographicCamera` in `MovingLeafBg`.

## Why

The leaf-grid board is flat in world space but viewed by a tilted camera (rotation `(25°,15°,9°)`), so the board spans a *range* of camera-space depth across the screen. Heavy browser zoom-out (`Cmd -`) grows the viewport in CSS pixels, which grows the visible footprint; because that footprint is raked relative to the view axis, its depth spread grows with it. Past a point the near edge swings *behind* the camera and the far edge pushes past `far`, so those strips get culled by the default `[0.1, 1000]` clip slab — the board stops covering the screen.

For an orthographic camera, apparent scale is set entirely by the frustum's `left/right/top/bottom`; `near`/`far` only control clipping. So widening the depth range (and using the legal negative `near`) fixes the culling with zero effect on how the scene looks.

## Test

`npm run dev`, zoom out hard with `Cmd -`: board now fills the viewport at all zoom levels, tiles otherwise unchanged.

author: cmalinmayor
body:
Currently, GraphArrayView invalidates the old and new bboxes in the cache any time any node attribute is updated, including totally unrelated ones.

Also, it appears that SQLGraph emits the signal that triggers this twice: https://github.com/royerlab/tracksdata/blob/13f9ba8f0a9376daaca5d388c7c979d8ca58f822/src/tracksdata/graph/_sql_graph.py#L2110-L2111 and https://github.com/royerlab/tracksdata/blob/13f9ba8f0a9376daaca5d388c7c979d8ca58f822/src/tracksdata/graph/_sql_graph.py#L2119-L2120

Every cache invalidation is expensive, and re-invaliding the same area multiple times resets any progress already made in loading.

This PR ensures the following behavior for all graph backends:
- If the spatial bbox and attr_key are unchanged, do not invalidate the cache
- If the spatial box is unchanged but the attr_key changes, invalidate the cache once
- If the spatial bbox is changed, invalidate the cache twice (old and new bboxes)

body:
## Summary

UX pass on the **Ecosystem Careers** board (`/ecosystem-careers`): open the listing up to everyone while gating the high-value details behind a connected X **and** LinkedIn.

Three changes:

1. **Top 15 instead of 3.** Visitors without both socials connected now see the top **15** roles in full — real, clickable cards, no blur wall — instead of 3. The wall of blurred cards is replaced by a single "connect to see all *N* roles" CTA panel.
2. **Salary is gated.** New optional `salary` field on listings, rendered as a pill on the card and the detail header, shown only to viewers with both X + LinkedIn connected. Everyone else sees a 🔒 *Salary* teaser.
3. **Click-through stays gated.** Opening a role still requires both socials to read the full description and apply (unchanged behaviour, just re-confirmed).

## Salary data model & sources

A single nullable `salary` column on `JobListing` — free-form, human-readable text (e.g. `$120k–$160k`, `$100k–$241k (est.)`). Populated from two places:

- **web3.career ingest (weekly cron).** Confirmed the API returns salary: `estimated_min/max_salary` are populated for ~82% of fetched roles, and the exact `salary_*_value` / `salary_currency` / `salary_unit` fields appear when employers provide them. The ingest prefers the exact employer range and falls back to the estimate, labelled `(est.)`.
- **Community submit/edit form.** New optional "Salary" input, surfaced only to signed-in candidates.

## Gating

Reuses the existing `canViewAll = hasX && hasLinkedIn` gate in `lib/ecosystem-careers/viewerAccess.ts`. `PUBLIC_JOB_PREVIEW_COUNT` goes 3 → 15. The detail page's existing description/Apply gate is unchanged; only the unlock copy now mentions salaries.

## What changed

- **Schema/migration** — `prisma/schema.prisma` + `20260603000000_add_job_listing_salary` (`ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "salary" TEXT`).
- **Read layer** — `salary` added to `JobCard` and mapped in `toJobCard` (`server/services/ecosystemCareers/queries.ts`).
- **Ingest** — `server/services/ecosystemCareers/ingestWeb3Career.ts`: typed the salary fields + `web3CareerSalary()` collapsing them into the single column.
- **Write path** — `listingSchema.ts`, `submitListing.ts`, `SubmitListingForm.tsx`, edit page `initialValues`.
- **UI** — `JobCard.tsx` (`showSalary` prop + pill/teaser), detail `[id]/page.tsx` header pill, `page.client.tsx` open-15 model, `UnlockPrompt.tsx` copy.

## ⚠️ Migration / deploy note

The migration adds one nullable column and is fully backward-compatible. It is **already applied to dev**. Migrations are **not** run in CI / the Vercel build, so **production needs a manual `prisma migrate deploy`** against the prod Neon branch before the salary display is relied on. (Existing rows stay `NULL`; salary lands on new external ingests and new/edited community listings.)

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- Applied the migration to the dev Neon branch; confirmed `salary` exists (`text`, nullable).
- Live web3.career call with the ingest's exact params: **82 / 100** fetched roles produced a salary string, e.g. `$108k–$250k (est.) · LayerZero Labs · Staff Solutions Architect`, `$190k–$225k (est.) · CoW DAO · Senior Backend Engineer (Rust)`.

## Reviewer notes

- Screenshots to add: the open 15-card board, a locked vs. unlocked salary card, and the detail header pill.
- web3.career salaries are mostly `(est.)` today (employers rarely fill the exact fields); the `(est.)` suffix keeps that honest.

author: atomantic
body:
Closes #740.

## What

Adds an opt-in env knob `PORTOS_T2V_TWO_STAGE` that routes the default **no-CFG** text-to-video Standard path through the two-stage pipeline (half-res stage 1 + latent upsample + short stage-2 refine) for a predicted ~30–35% wall-time reduction. This is the bounded first slice the issue asked for: ship the A/B knob now, validate quality on real prompts, then consider flipping two-stage on as the universal T2V Standard default in a follow-up.

## How

- `scripts/generate_ltx2.py` `run_text`: when `cfg_scale is None` **and** `PORTOS_T2V_TWO_STAGE` is truthy, route through `run_two_stage` with the fast experiment config (`stage1_steps=8`, `stage2_steps=3`, `cfg_scale=1.0`). Explicit `--steps` / `--stage2-steps` still win over the fast defaults.
- `run_two_stage` gained keyword-only overrides (`stage1_steps`/`stage2_steps`/`cfg_scale`/`status`) that default to `None` and fall back to the original CFG-path behavior — so the existing CFG callers (`run_image`, explicit `--cfg-scale`) are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- New `env_truthy()` helper (no existing one in `scripts/`).
- Default **off** → zero behavior change for anyone not opting in. No Node-side change needed: `safeChildProcessEnv` already spreads `process.env`, so the knob reaches the Python child.

## Verification

- `python3 -m py_compile scripts/generate_ltx2.py` passes.
- Full runtime A/B (quality on real prompts) is the maintainer's deferred follow-up per the issue — the knob is off by default and safe to ship.

body: ## Bug und Impact Parallele oder schnell hintereinander abgeschlossene Stripe-Checkout-Sessions konnten **zwei bezahlte Abonnements** für dieselbe Organisation erzeugen. In der Datenbank blieb nur ein `stripeSubscriptionId` erhalten — die Doppelbelastung blieb in Stripe bestehen. **Auslöser:** Org ohne `stripeSubscriptionId` in der DB (z. B. ticket: flow-aut.6
files:
  - plugins/flow/skills/flow/scripts/tracker_cli.py
  - plugins/flow/skills/flow/scripts/tests/test_tracker_cli.py
  - plugins/flow/skills/flow/references/stage-commit.md
  - plugins/flow/skills/flow/scripts/sync.py
  - plugins/flow/skills/flow/references/verb-sync-baseline.md
  - plugins/flow/skills/flow/scripts/tracker_beads.py

The pending-mutations queue (module + CLI + drain + /flow sync) was built and
tested but nothing ever wrote to it: append_mutation had zero non-test callers.
In an unattended run a transient network/auth blip on the commit-stage in_review
transition was logged and dropped permanently, and /flow sync could never
reconcile it because no write path existed.

Wire the enqueue at the one layer that holds the data needed to replay it: the
tracker_cli transition chokepoint, the only place with selected_id + fields +
key + to_state. The prose-level stages could not build a replayable entry.
Enqueue is opt-in via --enqueue-on-transient so only the commit-stage in_review
transition durably queues; the ticket-stage in_progress claim stays a re-runnable
double-pick guard and is left unqueued to avoid a backward-replay against a later
in_review. On a would-be exit 1 (raised TrackerError, or a returned
success=False with an unmapped failure_kind) the transition is appended as
op=transition with expected_postcondition={normalized: to_state}, which
round-trips through sync._invoke and the read-before-replay dedup. The enqueue is
best-effort: it never changes the transition's exit code. Hard failures (4/5),
no-transition (3), and success (0) never enqueue.

The adapters stay pure (raise TrackerError; the CLI seam owns durability), so the
stale phase-8 TODO in tracker_beads is folded, and the sync.py / verb-sync prose
that falsely claimed the queue was "written by adapter failure paths" now names
the real writer.

Re-cut clean off main (original dogfood PR #24 was on a stale base — flow-mvz). Tracks flow-aut.6 (P1 data-loss).

body:
## Summary

Inventory the diary `new` and `edit` screens in screen-parity (#62), recording the web-public visibility gap I flagged while landing #63.

**Ground truth (verified against OpenPNE 3, not assumed):** `PluginDiaryForm` renders `public_flag` as a radio whose choices come from `DiaryTable::getPublicFlags()`. By default that list includes `PUBLIC_FLAG_OPEN` → "All Users on the Web" (gated by SNS config `op_diary_plugin_use_open_diary`, default on); `is_open` is derived from picking that choice, not a separate checkbox. The Classic new/edit form offers only members/friends/private, so **a member cannot post a web-public diary** — even though show now renders one correctly (#63).

Adds `new` and `edit` to `DiaryRouteParity::screens()` with the full form element set, surfacing:
- ❌ web-public (Open) visibility option — the headline gap
- ❌ remembered default visibility (member config); 🟡 rich-text body editor; 🚫 image upload / image edit; ❌ LayoutB + sidemenu; ❌ delete box (edit places delete on the show page instead)

`DiaryFormParityTest` locks the ported visibility choice and pins the *absence* of the web-public option, so when the gap is closed a failing assertion prompts flipping the inventory element to ported.

## Test plan

- `php artisan openpne:screen-parity` renders `page_diary_new` / `page_diary_edit` with the web-public option as ❌ missing.
- `DiaryFormParityTest`: new form offers members/friends/private, does not yet offer "Public to Web"; edit preselects the diary's visibility.

author: satyakwok
body:
## Summary

Adds `reliakit-backoff`, a clock-agnostic retry backoff library. It computes how long to wait between retries and never sleeps or reads the clock, so it works in synchronous code, any async runtime, and `no_std` / embedded contexts.

- `Backoff` — `constant` / `linear` / `exponential` strategies with `with_max_delay` and `with_max_retries`; `delay(attempt)` and a `delays()` iterator.
- `full_jitter` / `equal_jitter` — pure helpers that take a caller-supplied random value (no RNG dependency).
- `#![no_std]`, zero dependencies, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`; builds for bare-metal `thumbv7em-none-eabi`.

## Tests

16 unit tests plus doc tests; the full feature matrix and the bare-metal `no_std` build pass. Exponential `delay()` with a zero base (or an already-saturated delay) returns promptly instead of iterating the full attempt count, with a regression test covering `delay(u32::MAX)`.

author: alastair87
body:
## Problem

When `data/incomplete/` and `data/models/` are on different filesystem mount points, the final step of a download fails with:

```
[Errno 18] Invalid cross-device link: 'data/incomplete/...' -> 'data/models/...'
```

`os.replace()` (like `os.rename()`) cannot move files across device boundaries — it only works within the same filesystem.

## Fix

Replace `os.replace()` with `shutil.move()` in `app/services/downloader.py`.

`shutil.move()` attempts `os.rename()` first for efficiency, and falls back to `copy2()` + `unlink()` when a cross-device error (EXDEV / errno 18) is raised. Safe on both single- and multi-device setups with no behavioural regression.

## Changes

- `app/services/downloader.py` — add `import shutil`; replace `os.replace()` with `shutil.move()`
- `tests/test_downloader.py` (new) — two tests verifying correct behaviour and cross-device fallback

author: ashwinsreedhar28
body:
## What changed
`nodes/lanes/` now reports two extra fields per lane on `lanes.status`, for the upcoming Lanes view: `last_commit_msg` (the HEAD commit subject) and `pr` (`{ number, state, url }` for the lane's branch), plus a top-level `gh_available` flag. The git-derived `last_commit_msg` rides the existing 10s git tick; the GitHub-derived `pr` is fetched on a separate, slower, fully-decoupled 60s cadence and merged into the payload at serve time. No other packages touched; the visualizer's `renderLanes` is intentionally untouched (the Lanes view is a separate consumer lane).

## Why
The upcoming Lanes view needs each lane's latest commit subject and its PR state (open/merged/closed + link). Per the lane spec, the enrichment must not change the sensor's cost profile: GitHub is never consulted on the fast git tick, and a slow/failing/absent `gh` must degrade silently without crashing the sensor or stalling the git poll.

## How (high level)
- **`last_commit_msg`** gathered in the existing 10s `collectLane` git call — one combined `git log -1 --format=%ct%n%s` yields both commit time and subject, so no extra process spawn. `null` when the worktree has no commits. The `main` worktree gets it too.
- **`pr`** resolved in a new async `collectPRs()` (`src/gh.ts`) via `gh pr list --state all --json number,state,url,headRefName` (`--state all` so merged/closed PRs still resolve; `state` passed through verbatim). Multi-PR-per-branch tie-break: an `OPEN` PR wins, else the highest number — deterministic.
- **Separate 60s cadence**, cached in node state, merged into the served payload by branch at serve time. `pr` is null for `main` (is_main), for branches with no PR, and whenever gh is unavailable. The gh call is `execFile` (async), so a slow GitHub round trip never blocks the cached-status serve or the git poll.
- **Silent degrade**: gh missing / unauthenticated / network error / malformed JSON all collapse to `{ available: false }` → every `pr` null + top-level `gh_available: false`. Never throws.

## Risks / TODOs / Skipped
- The Lanes-view rendering of these fields ("—" for absent/null) is a separate lane; this PR only produces the contract.
- `gh pr list` is capped at `--limit 300` (default is 30); this repo has 130+ PRs under `--state all`. Generous headroom, but a hard cap nonetheless — noted for when it's eventually exceeded.
- No unit tests added (week-1 / sensor-node convention); verified via headless smoke instead (see Verification).

## Out-of-scope work explicitly avoided
- Visualizer `renderLanes` panel — left as-is per locked decision; the Lanes view is the consumer, a separate lane.
- Did not shorten either polling interval (git 10s / PR 60s) — locked.
- No live CC-process detection — remains the documented future enhancement from the original sensor.

## Pre-PR heuristics
- **§11.1 semantic ordering** — N/A (no new user-facing ordered lists).
- **§11.3 code/comment accuracy** — comments state the combined `git log` avoids a second spawn; the `%ct%n%s` format and single-line `%s` assumption verified.
- **§11.6 reserve space** — `gh --limit 300` leaves headroom; tie-break rule is explicit rather than positional.
- **§11.7 cross-platform** — no platform-specific code; `gh`/`git` are cross-platform CLIs.
- **§11.8 _ingest simplification** — N/A (no pattern lifted).
- **§11.9 cross-doc consistency** — README, schema description, and CHANGELOG updated as one surface; params schema deliberately unchanged (surface takes no params — confirmed against sibling node schemas, which are params-schemas with response shape in prose).
- **§11.10 load-bearing decisions** — wire contract (field names, null semantics, `gh_available`, gh state passthrough) pre-committed in the spec; non-load-bearing choices (combined-log spawn-saving, tie-break rule, `--limit`) decided at write-time and documented here + in code comments.

## Verification
Headless, no GUI required. `pnpm -r build / typecheck / lint` clean across all 17 workspace packages.

Ran the compiled collectors directly:
- **last_commit_msg** — populated for all worktrees including `main` (`pr: null` for main).
- **PR resolution (gh present)** — `gh_available: true`, 103 branches resolved; `feat/voice-lanes-intent → { number: 131, state: "MERGED", url: ... }` — MERGED state passes through, proving `--state all`. A branch with no PR resolves to `null`.
- **gh absent** — ran with a PATH symlinked to `node` only (no `gh`): `gh_available: false`, zero PRs, clean exit in **3ms** — no crash, no stall, fast degrade.
- **Schema** — `nodes/lanes/schemas/status.json` validates as Draft 2020-12; the no-params request payload `{}` validates and an extra-prop payload is correctly rejected.

Re-verified post-rebase onto `origin/main` (picks up #132): lanes build clean, smoke holds (`main`'s `last_commit_msg` now reflects #132's subject, confirming it tracks HEAD).

## Open questions for Architect
None.

author: bkaradzic-microsoft
body:
## Problem

`NativeEngine::ReadTexture` validates the destination ArrayBuffer with:

```cpp
if (buffer.ByteLength() < bufferOffset + bufferLength)
```

`bufferOffset` and `bufferLength` are both JS-supplied `uint32_t` (from `engine.readTexture(...)`), so `bufferOffset + bufferLength` is evaluated in **32-bit** and can wrap around before being promoted to `size_t` for the comparison. For example `bufferOffset = 0xF0000000` and `bufferLength = 0x20000000` wrap to `0x10000000` (256 MiB) and pass the check against any sufficiently large buffer. The subsequent `storageSize > bufferLength` gate also passes (the real pixel payload is small), and the async continuation then runs:

```cpp
std::memcpy(buffer + bufferOffset, textureBuffer.data(), textureBuffer.size());
```

writing the pixel data at the out-of-range `bufferOffset` and overflowing the ArrayBuffer backing store (heap OOB write, CWE-190 → CWE-787).

## Fix

Widen the addition to 64-bit so `bufferOffset + bufferLength` can't wrap:

```cpp
if (buffer.ByteLength() < static_cast<uint64_t>(bufferOffset) + bufferLength)
```

With the existing `storageSize <= bufferLength` gate, this guarantees `bufferOffset + storageSize <= ByteLength` before the memcpy.

## Testing

- win32 D3D11 Debug: Playground validation suite `ran=160 passed=160 failed=0` (every screenshot pixel comparison exercises `ReadTexture`).

author: zeveck
body:
## Summary
Closes #1055. **Security fix (Medium)** — credential/PII leak vector.

The session-logging hooks (shipped by PR #1053) wrote transcripts (verbatim prompts, Bash tool I/O including any cat-ed credentials, WebFetch URLs with tokens, permission decisions) with the **default process umask** → mode **0o644 (world-readable)** under the typical umask 022. On multi-user systems with a shared `/tmp`, any local user could read another user's session log.

## Fix (file mode only — no behavior change)
- `hooks/log-session-stop.sh` — `os.umask(0o077)` as the first statement of `main()`, before any file creation, so the `.tmp` write, the `os.replace` final markdown, and `makedirs` all land **0o600** (closes the tmp-window race, not a post-hoc chmod).
- `hooks/log-permission-request.sh` — same `os.umask(0o077)`, plus belt-and-suspenders explicit-mode sidecar creation: `os.open(sidecar, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_APPEND, 0o600)`.
- Mirrors `.claude/hooks/*` updated byte-identically; hook-version stamp bumped `2026.06.0`→`2026.06.1` (source + mirror).
- Verbatim capture, atomic rename, append semantics, and fail-open are all unchanged — only the mode tightens.

## Test plan
- [x] `tests/test-session-logging.sh` Case 6 (3 assertions): Stop markdown 0o600, permission sidecar 0o600, tmp-window 0o600. Hooks are exercised under a relaxed `umask 022` subshell, so the assertions **fail against the old 0o644 code** (real regression guards, independently verified non-tautological).
- [x] Full suite **7634/7634** passing; `test-hooks-mirror-parity.sh` 30/0.
- [x] No skill `metadata.version` bump — the hooks live in `hooks/`, not under a skill dir, so the skill content hash is unchanged; hook changes are tracked by the hook-version stamp. (The issue's bump line assumed the hooks were under the skill dir.)

## What

Phase -1 of the git-parity roadmap (#247, umbrella #246): the **scope gate**.
Adds the authoritative parity matrix and a differential test harness scaffold.
No behavior changes to mkit — docs + a new test file only.

### `docs/PARITY.md`
- Scope statement (CLI/UX parity only; BLAKE3/native formats remain) + the two inherent divergences (hash length, repo marker).
- Explicit **v1 non-goals** list (submodules, hooks, multi-worktree, full refspec grammar, protocol v2, `notes`, `.git/` interop) so v1 scope can't creep.
- Command matrix: `command | git-compatible subset | mkit current state | status | phase | issue | notes`, statuses ✅ shipped / 📝 docs-only gap / 🔨 to implement / 🚫 non-goal.
- Safety-divergence section (the mkit guards we keep) + machine-output contract for agents/scripts.

### `rust/crates/mkit-cli/tests/git_parity_harness.rs`
- Runs the same script under real `git` and `mkit` in isolated repos (neutralized HOME/global config; pinned git identity; canonicalized temp root to dodge the macOS `/var` symlink during signed commits).
- Normalizes output **modulo object-id length** (40-hex SHA-1 vs 64-hex BLAKE3).
- **Passing subset enforced today:** `status --porcelain=v1` parity (untracked / staged-add / staged-modification) + a clean-repo smoke + a normalizer unit test.
- **Pending rows** (`status --porcelain=v2` #249, unified `diff` #257, `log --oneline` #248) are `#[ignore]`d with their phase/issue, carrying the full comparison so un-ignoring is a one-line change when the feature lands.
- Skips (passes) when no real `git` is on PATH.

## CI

No `rust.yml` change needed — `cargo nextest run` picks up the new test file on Ubuntu + macOS and skips `#[ignore]`d cases by default, so only the passing subset is enforced. Verified locally: `5 passed, 3 skipped`; clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean.

## Out of scope (later phases)

Implementing any 🔨 row — those are owned by #248–#260. This PR only establishes the gate and the harness they assert against.
